body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-15:

> Bug, when cutting a countour, setting a boundary or "inside" / "outside" either generates errors or are not respected. The centerline of the tool is not offset from the edge selection, and cuts straight thru the part of the model that is supposed to be left behind.

What happens:
- A Contour operation has an edge selection.
- The user sets the side to Inside or Outside, or sets a boundary.
- Generate gives an error, or the side and the boundary have no effect.
- The tool centre line runs on the picked edge. It is not offset by the tool radius.
- The pass cuts through the part of the model that must stay.

Expected:
- The tool centre line is offset from the picked edge by the tool radius, to the side the user set.
- A boundary limits the pass.
- A pass that cuts the model is a gouge and blocks the post.

Not known yet:
- The exact error texts.
- The model and the picks (open edges or a closed loop). The maintainer works with `Block-w-slot.step`.
- If the gouge check reports this pass. If it does not, wrong G-code can be posted. The priority is P1 for that reason. Lower it to P3 if the post is blocked.

Related: #1726, #1727, #1735 (open edge selections).

Done means:
- A test reproduces the case with an edge selection and each side value.
- The tool centre line is one tool radius from the edge on the set side, and the pass does not cut the model.
- A boundary limits the pass, or the operation is refused by name.
- A test shows that a Contour pass through the model blocks the post.

title: 3D Pocket open sides: tilted (3+2) ops and stock far past the silhouette still leave stock while reporting ok

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Follow-up of #1749 (draft PR #1772). Found by the #1749 worker and filed by SKULL.

**What happens.** PR #1772 grows an untilted whole-model 3D Pocket's footprint by the tool radius (less 0.01 mm) where a level is open to air. Two cases are still outside that change and can leave stock standing while the op reports `ok`:

1. **A tilted (3+2) 3D Pocket** still uses the old footprint, the silhouette shrunk by the tool radius. An open-sided notch keeps a band one radius wide at full stock height, which is the #1749 ridge.
2. **Stock reaching more than about two tool radii past the silhouette** is not cleared on an open side. The grown footprint stops at the silhouette edge plus about a radius.

**What must happen.** Either the open side is cleared out to the stock outline, as the 2D pocket has done since #12, with no cutter position entering any part; or the op names the uncleared band in a warning, or is marked incomplete. It must never read `ok` over standing stock.

**Done means**
- A pinning test for each case, built in code like `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_open_side.rs`. It measures the carried stock along the open edge and requires either the floor or a named warning or incomplete.
- A gouge check: no cutter position inside a part.
- Each new line mutation-checked.

Part of #1749's area. See `docs/decisions/1749-pocket3d-open-side.md` on PR #1772's branch.

labels.name: enhancement

labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.description: Large idea with open questions: research and file sub-issues before any code

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
**The request (the user, 2026-11-14):** "create an ai chat window in CamCraft that would interact with ai thru mcp or whatever appropriate. Make sure that we help those agents with appropriate skill stuff for various ai tools like Claude, codex, Gemini, unsloth, ollama, etc."

This is a research umbrella (`needs-research`). It answers the open questions below in comments. Then it files the concrete sub-issues and closes. No code goes on this issue.

## What exists today

- `camcraft-cli mcp` is an MCP server on stdio. An agent drives one headless document.
- The app can start with `--mcp-port`, and `camcraft-cli mcp --connect <host:port>` bridges an external agent to the open window. The agent then drives the live document.
- The skill `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/` documents the tools for Claude Code.
- Every MCP tool calls the same undoable commands as the GUI (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool").

## Goal

1. **In-app chat panel.** A dock panel in CamCraft where the user types a request, for example "add a 2D pocket on the selected face with T3". An AI model answers and acts through the same MCP tool set. The panel shows each tool call and its result.
2. **Provider choice.** The user picks the model provider and the model:
   - **Cloud:** Anthropic (Claude), OpenAI (GPT/Codex models), Google (Gemini).
   - **Local:** Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio, llama.cpp server (most local servers have an OpenAI-compatible API).
3. **External agents.** Each external agent tool gets one documented way to drive the open app (`--mcp-port` plus `mcp --connect`), and a skill or instruction file in its own format:
   - Claude Code: `.claude/skills/` (exists; keep it current);
   - Codex CLI: AGENTS.md section or `.codex/` instructions;
   - Gemini / Antigravity CLI: `GEMINI.md` and `.agents/skills/`;
   - local models through Ollama or Unsloth: a short system prompt plus the tool list.

## Open questions (answer each in a comment)

1. **Panel architecture.** In-process, where the app calls the provider API and maps the MCP tools to the provider's tool-calling format? Or a separate process that speaks MCP to the app? What keeps the UI thread free (async, cancel)?
2. **One tool schema for all providers.** Map the MCP tool schemas to the Anthropic Messages tool format, the OpenAI tools format, and Gemini function declarations. Which local models do tool calling well enough? What is the fallback for a model without tool calling?
3. **Safety.**
   - Every action goes through the undoable commands.
   - The chat never posts G-code, never writes a file, and never changes a machine without a confirmation in the panel.
   - Group one chat turn as one undo step, or one step per command?
   - How does the panel show what changed?
4. **Keys and privacy.**
   - Where do API keys live (the OS keychain)?
   - What is sent to a cloud model (the project data, the model geometry)?
   - How does an offline-only setting work (local models only)?
5. **Context size.** How does a large project (many operations, big meshes) fit a model's context window? Summaries, on-demand tool reads?
6. **Skills per tool.** One source of truth for the tool docs (generated from the MCP tool list?) with per-tool wrappers, so the docs never drift from the shipped tools.
7. **Tests.** Test the panel and the tool mapping without network access (a scripted fake provider).
8. **Clean room.** Only public API documentation of each provider and the MCP specification. No code or prompts copied from other CAM products.

## Sub-issues to file (when the research is done)

- The chat panel: UI, history, tool-call display, cancel, confirmation prompts.
- The provider adapters: Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, and OpenAI-compatible local (Ollama, Unsloth, LM Studio, llama.cpp).
- The tool-schema mapping, generated from the MCP tool list.
- Keys and privacy settings, plus the offline mode.
- Skill and instruction files for Claude Code, Codex, Gemini/Antigravity and local models, generated from one source.
- Docs (REQUIRED): "Use AI with CamCraft": setup and worked examples for every provider (Claude, OpenAI/Codex, Gemini, Ollama, Unsloth Studio, LM Studio, llama.cpp) and every external agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini/Antigravity CLI, headless). See the comment that adds docs to the scope.

**Done means:** every open question has an answered comment, every sub-issue is filed with "Part of #this", and this umbrella is closed.

title: Mask tests: compare a generated toolpath with its described shape

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
The maintainer asked for this in chat (2026-11-15):

> is it possible to use the cli tool to verify tool paths "visually".. we know what they should look like mathematically.. could we inspect them using rasterized tests?

> Idea is to sanity checks that changes to the motion crates actually gets implemented as described by the user

## Problem

A change to a toolpath generator is described in words in its issue (for example "the pass extends to the stock edge", "the corners are arcs", "the slot is cleared with trochoidal loops"). The tests of the change pin numbers that the author chose. No test compares the shape of the generated toolpath with the shape that the description gives. A change can pass its tests and not do what the user described.

## Proposal

Add a test helper that compares two masks on one grid:

- The expected region. The test builds it from the mathematical description (an outline, a depth, an extension).
- The swept region. The helper builds it from the tool footprint along the generated toolpath.

The helper gives these assertions:

- No overcut: no swept cell is outside the expected region, within one cell.
- Bounded leftover: the uncut area is below a stated limit, and the uncut cells are only in stated places.
- Engagement: no move cuts a width larger than the stated stepover.
- Shape laws: symmetry for a symmetric region, and no move outside the stock plus the stated extension.

When an assertion fails, the helper writes the difference mask as a PNG file into the test output folder. A person can then see where the toolpath is wrong. The test result comes from the numbers, not from an image comparison. No PNG golden is stored.

## Rules

- The helper is test code. It does not change a generator, a gouge check or a collision check.
- The helper is in the crate that owns the toolpath types (`crates/motion`), and uses the CPU rasteriser or its own grid. It does not need a GPU.
- The grid limits the precision to one cell. Exact laws (arc radius, depth, feed words) stay as numeric tests.
- A PR that changes a 2D generator in `crates/motion` adds or updates one mask test that states the described shape.

## First users

- Trochoidal slot.
- 2D Adaptive.
- The open-edge region of issue 1735 and the Slot extension of issue 1731.

Done means: the helper is in the repository with its own unit tests; the trochoidal slot and 2D Adaptive each have one mask test that fails when the generator is changed to overcut or to leave too much material (shown by a mutation check in the PR); a failed assertion writes the difference PNG; AGENTS.md "Testing" names the helper.

Found during the work on issue 1735.

## Problem

Issue 1735 made two open edges a band that the stock outline closes. When the two edges, run on straight, meet inside the stock, the band has one open end only. The operation refuses that selection by name: "the two picked open edges run together inside the stock - the band between them has one open end only ...". Edges at more than 45 degrees to each other are also refused.

## Wanted

- Decide if a wedge between two edges that meet inside the stock is a valid region.
- If it is valid, define the region exactly and write the definition in a decision record.
- Decide if the 45 degree limit stays.

body:
Found during the work on issue 1735.

## Problem

A blind slot has two side walls and one end wall. The user picks the three top edges as one U-shaped open run. A pocket-family operation (2D Offset, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive) refuses the selection: "... is an open run - a 2D Offset cannot end mid-edge ...".

Issue 1735 made two separate open edges a band that the stock outline closes. One open run with one open side is not covered.

## Wanted

- One U-shaped open run is a region with one open side. The stock outline closes the open side.
- The extension moves the open side out of the stock along the two end tangents of the run.
- A run whose region is not clear is refused by name.

## Safety

The gouge check and the collision check must not change. A pass that cuts a kept part must block the post. Pin that with a test that expects the refusal.

## Done means

A pocket-family operation on a blind slot picked as one open run generates a path from the end wall to the stock edge, with a pinning test and a refusal test.

Part of the work that started with #1735.

body:
Part of #1733.

The fix for #1733 adds the corner arc radius to the arc turns option of these kinds:

- 2D Pocket
- 2D Adaptive (Spiral method; the Trochoidal method refuses the option by name)
- 2D Offset

These kinds do not have the option yet:

- Slot. Open PR #1745 (issue 1731) changes Slot. Do this work after PR #1745 merges, so that the two PRs do not conflict.
- Face.
- 2D Contour. A contour follows the wall, so a rounded corner can leave material on an outside corner. Examine which corners can turn on an arc in the region the sharp pass cuts.

Use the same parameters as the three kinds above: `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. No radius means the tool radius. The bound and the refusal text are in `camcraft_motion::machining2d::corner_arc_radius` and in `crates/app/src/operation/types/sane.rs`.

Done means:
- Each kind that can round its corners safely has the option and the radius as operation parameters. The undoable parameter command and MCP `edit_operation` set them.
- A toolpath test for each kind pins the corners as tangent arcs of the given radius, and pins that no arc cuts past the wall.
- The default output of each kind does not change. No golden changes.
- A kind that cannot round its corners safely is named in the PR with the reason.

title: 3D Pocket on a notch open to the part's outside leaves tall ridges along the open edge (op says ok)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: in-review
labels.description: Fix pushed on a branch with an open PR; merges at the next cut

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
**What happens.** A whole-model 3D Pocket clears a notch that is open to the part's outside: a quadrant step in the side of a block. It leaves tall ridges of stock along the part's outer edge at the notch, because the cutter stays inside the model boundary. The op reports `ok`. The next setup then refuses the post, correctly: `fixture '…' stands inside the stock carried from setup 'Setup 1' (9.93 mm deep)`.

**Numbers (CamCraft v0.20.0, a user's two-sided part).**
- The part is a 30 mm cube made of two L halves, with R3.125 fillets. Setup 1 cuts the top notch with a 3D Pocket: whole model, shell on, offset rings, a 6.35 mm flat end mill, 2.032 mm stepover, 0.15 mm stepdown, 0 stock to leave. The floor is Z 19.826.
- In the middle of the notch, the carried stock is cut to the floor, as expected.
- Near the notch's open edges (for example X 14.81 at the part edge), the carried stock stays at Z 33.326 and 34.676, about 14-15 mm above the floor. The finished model there is at about Z 18-19.
- The flip into Setup 2 and the fixture positions are correct. The fixtures clear the finished model by 1.0 to 3.6 mm. The carried-stock check measures the uncut ridge correctly.

**Expected.** Either the pocket clears an open-sided notch to the part's outer edge (the open side is air, so the cutter may go past the model boundary into the stock), or the op says by name that it leaves material along an open edge, and how much.

**Workaround today.** A machining boundary or a stock-source region that reaches past the part's edge at the open sides. Not yet tested.

**Done means:** a 3D Pocket on a block with an open-sided quadrant notch leaves no material above the floor plus the stock to leave at the open edges, pinned by a test. Or the op names the material it leaves.

Found while making a two-sided job (soft jaws in Setup 2). The user's files stay private.

body:
**What happens.** In a second setup that holds the part turned (part alignment, for example flipped 180° about X), 3D operations are refused. The message is: `setup 'Setup 2' holds the part turned (part alignment) - 3D Pocket is not supported yet in an aligned setup (Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive are)`. A flipped setup also refuses picks and area controls.

**Where the user hits it.** A 30 mm cube with R3.125 mm fillets on every edge, machined from two sides. Setup 1 can finish the top fillets. The bottom fillets and the bottom-notch floor fillets need 3D work in the flipped Setup 2, so today they stay unmachined (2D only).

**Expected.** 3D Pocket and 3D Finish (and 3D Adaptive) generate in a flipped setup: in the setup's own frame, judged against the part as that setup holds it, with the same gouge laws as an unturned setup. A pose that the generator cannot handle is refused by name.

**Related.** #763 (one machining-frame seam: OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame) is the groundwork. #874 is the side-on (90°) case.

**Done means:** a 3D Pocket and a 3D Finish on a part flipped 180° about X generate, verify and post. The pins show no gouge on the flipped part, and the path is identical to the same op on the unflipped part, mapped through the flip.

body:
Reported by the maintainer in chat, 2026-11-14:

> bug; when selecting twwo edges and clicking 2D generate on a 2D operation i get the error "generate failed: could not generate the toolpath: 2D Offset1: invalid machining parameters: edge chain 0x148aab7f74e64a39 of 'Block-w-slot' is an open run - a 2D Offset cannot end mid-edge; select a closed chain - Ctrl+click the remaining edges, or Shift+click to take the whole loop" - this should not be the case. It should generate path up to the edge of the stock.. And the Extend past - should extend that reach outside of the stock in the direction of the edges..

What happens:
- The geometry selection of a 2D Offset holds two open edges of the model `Block-w-slot`.
- Generate refuses the operation with the message above.

What must happen:
- Two open edges are the walls of a region with open ends.
- The operation cuts the region between the two edges. The open ends reach to the edge of the stock.
- The parameter "Extend past" moves each open end out of the stock, in the direction of the edges.
- The tool does not go around the corner at the end of an edge.

Evidence:
- `crates/app/src/operation/selection.rs` (`selection_geometry_in`): the Pocket family, Trace and Engrave refuse an open edge run. See the worker's finding in issue 1726 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/1726#issuecomment-6885264345).
- Issue 1726 now tracks only the pick defect (the first Ctrl+click does not add the second edge). This issue tracks the toolpath.

Safety:
- The two edges are walls. The gouge check must judge the new moves against the model. A cut into the part must block the post.
- A selection that does not give a clear region (edges that are not opposite, one edge only, edges at different heights) must be refused with a message that names the cause.

Done means:
- A 2D Offset, a 2D Pocket and a 2D Adaptive with two opposite open edges generate a toolpath between the edges, up to the stock edge.
- "Extend past" moves the open ends out of the stock, and a test pins the distance.
- A test shows that the tool does not cut past a wall edge.
- A test shows that an unclear selection is refused by name.

title: Pocket, Slot and similar operations: add an option for arc turns at the corners of the passes

labels.name: area:ui

body:
Reported by the maintainer (2026-11-14, in chat): "all passes should have Arc Turns at corners as an option when the operation is a type like pocket, slot, etc etc."

What happens: the passes of the area operations (Pocket, Slot and the same kind of operation) have sharp corners. The operation has no option to make the tool turn a corner on an arc.

Expected:
- Each operation of this kind has an option for arc turns at the corners of its passes, with a radius parameter.
- With the option on, the tool moves through a corner on an arc that is tangent to the two moves. The post writes the arc as `G2` or `G3` where the post supports arcs.
- The default keeps the output of existing programs. The worker lists the operation kinds that get the option in the PR.

Safety: an arc turn changes the toolpath. The arc must stay on the air side of the wall and inside the cut region. The gouge check must judge the result. Material that an arc turn leaves in a corner must not be left silently: the operation must cut it or report it.

Done means: the option and the radius are operation parameters, set through the undoable parameter command and the MCP tool `edit_operation`; a toolpath test for each operation kind pins that the corners are tangent arcs of the given radius; a test pins that no arc cuts past the wall; the default output of existing golden programs does not change.

title: finish3d: a straight link across gap openings (gap_link: Jump, Straight)

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: claimed
labels.description: An agent is working on this - see the claim comment

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
What the user asked for (chat, 2026-11-14): "i want it to form a smooth link move over holes in the surface. lets start with a straight line between each edge of the hole. later we can add splines and curves for how to connect them."

What happens now: finish3d (Parallel and the other march patterns) breaks a raster line where the tool cannot stand, for example over a hole. The chain between the two runs lifts to the retract plane. The tool makes an air hop for every gap. On a part with many holes this is slow and the moves look wrong in the GUI.

Change: add an operation parameter `gap_link` to the finishing parameters. The parameter is a dropdown with two options:

- `Jump` (default): today's behaviour, unchanged. The chain lifts to the retract plane.
- `Straight`: one straight Feed move between the end of one run and the start of the next, at the two end points' own tip height.

Law for `Straight`: both run ends stand at tangent centers by the march construction. The author certifies the exact segment-triangle sweep of the move at the budget `r - TOUCH_EPS`. A grazing contact at the rim passes. A real bite refuses. On a refusal the chain takes the `Jump` hop. No air margin is added for `Straight`; `Jump` keeps its own retract law.

Also fixed, needed by this feature: the raster serpentine ran a broken back line wrong. It reversed only each piece's points and kept the pieces in grid order. Every gap link then jumped back across the field instead of crossing its gap. A back line now reverses whole: the pieces in reverse order, and each piece's points reversed. This also shortens the existing `Jump` traverses on broken lines.

How the parameter is stored: the project digest takes a `0x4D` tag plus a variant byte only when `gap_link` is not `Jump`. The project file grammar takes the words `jump` and `straight`. No project-file version step-up. The MCP params door and the UI combo carry the same two options.

Done means:

- The Gap link dropdown offers Jump and Straight; Jump is the default and writes the old bytes.
- Over a holed plate, `Straight` authors rim-to-rim Feed links at the run height and no retract hop for those gaps.
- A `Straight` link that would cut the part is refused, and the hop stands (Prime Directive).
- Every gap crossing on a broken back line spans one gap, never the field.
- Pins: `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_gaplink.rs`, the round-trip pins in `crates/app/tests/project_roundtrip.rs`, and the MCP params-door test.

body:
What happens: the release gate of the v0.20.0 cut is red in the kernel suites. The test `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name` (`crates/kernel/tests/step_agreement.rs`) fails on `testdata/models/bspline_discontinuous.step`.

Evidence (local release gate, Windows, head `182b7018a`, log `gate-logs/release-20261114-185541/02-kernel_suites.log`):

```
thread 'step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name' panicked at crates\kernel\tests\step_util\mod.rs:56:19:
bspline_discontinuous.step: no answer 30s after its cancel (timed out waiting on channel) - a hang or a panic
test result: FAILED. 0 passed; 1 failed; ... finished in 90.46s
```

The reader did not answer in the time limit and did not answer 30 s after the cancel. The files before it in the list (`Block-w-slot.step`, `Milling-test-inch.step`, `Milling-test.step`, `bad_entity_mid_data.step`, `box.step`) gave an answer.

Expected: a degenerate STEP file gives a named refusal in the time limit, or the reader obeys the cancel. A hang on an input file is against the Prime Directive.

Not known: which reader hangs (solidcore, truck or the tessellation), and if the cause is the file or the load of the gate on the machine. The batch gate on main `4f4edcf35` did not run this suite (kernel runs in the release tier only).

Done means:
- The cause is named.
- `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name` passes in the release tier.
- A reader that hangs on this file refuses it by name or obeys the cancel, with a test that pins it.

body:
What happens: the local batch gate on main `4f4edcf35` fails two app tests. The post refuses two legal stock-source cuts.

Evidence (`cargo xtask gate batch`, log `07-app_suites`):

1. `-p camcraft-app --test stock_source_cross_drill`, test `a_stock_source_cross_drill_at_the_modelled_holes_size_is_excused_its_faceted_wall`, `crates/app/tests/stock_source_cross_drill.rs:211`:
```
bar turned false: posts: post blocked - stock sim did not judge this program: S1: move 1: posed moves are not modelled by the column engine (its atoms stand upright on +Z; a tilted tool cut upright is a wrong verdict) - and S1 now cuts part 'bar' (move 1 cuts past the finish surface) - a part moved, added or no longer workholding since it was generated; regenerate it
```
2. `-p camcraft-app --test stock_source_holes`, test `a_hole_kind_in_the_parts_own_hole_or_in_stock_only_material_posts`, `crates/app/tests/stock_source_holes_support/mod.rs:333`:
```
drill-in-hole-true: a legal stock-source cut posts: post blocked - stock sim did not judge this program: the program sim models an axis-aligned stock; this stock carries a rotation - and S1 now cuts part 'part' (move 1 cuts past the finish surface) - a part moved, added or no longer workholding since it was generated; regenerate it
```

Probable cause (not confirmed): the live judgment of kept parts at the post (PR 1643) does not apply the excuses that the generation-time judgment gives to a stock-source hole cut (PR 1634, PR 1640, PR 1644). A drill in the part's own modelled hole is then reported as a cut into the part.

Expected: the post gives the same verdict as the generation-time judgment for an unchanged document. A real cut into a part must still block the post.

This holds the v0.20.0 release gate.

Done means: the two tests pass, and a pinning test shows that a stock-source drill which cuts solid part material is still refused at the post.

body:
Found in the review of PR #1670 (#1664). The same point applies to PR #1663 (#1609).

**What happens.** A Ramp entry with no entry ramp angle uses the links' ramp angle (`links.ramp_angle`). This is the angle of the ramps between passes. When a user sets a large link angle, for example 45°, the entry ramp also becomes 45°. A steep chord is then kept at the cutting feed. The ramp angle of the entry and the ramp angle of the links are two different settings in practice.

**Expected.** The Ramp entry has its own angle, with a safe default (3°). The links keep their angle. Alternatively, the entry uses the smaller of the two angles.

**Done means:** the entry angle of Contour (side Inside), Circular and Bore does not follow a large link angle. A pin shows that a 45° link angle gives an entry at no more than the entry angle.

title: STL/OBJ import: a closed body wound inward keeps a negative volume, nothing says so

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## Problem

PR #1671 turns a closed STEP body that is wound inward outward at import, and says so. The STL and OBJ importers do not do this. An inward closed STL or OBJ body keeps a negative signed volume.

`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/pencil.rs` and `deburr.rs` use the facet winding to tell a concave edge from a convex edge. An inward body swaps the two. Pencil can then trace convex edges, and deburr can select concave corners. No gouge path is known. The heights were not examined.

## Done means

- A closed, consistently wound STL or OBJ body with a negative signed volume imports turned outward, with a note in the import result and on the status line. Or the import refuses it with a clear message.
- A pinning test for each format.
- The trace of pencil and deburr heights for an inward body is recorded on this issue.

Part of the work that #1617 started.

title: Verify: a rim-vertex crossing uses an exact sign test, so a wall that runs along the trace with a small wobble counts as a crossing

labels.name: effort:high

labels.name: P7

body:
Found in M5's review of PR #1668 (#1659). The review did not block on it.

## What happens

`crosses_rim` (`crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs`) counts a pass through a loop vertex as a rim crossing when the vertex's two neighbours lie on opposite sides of the move. The test is the exact sign `su * sw < 0`, with no zero band.

Assume a wall that runs along the trace and wobbles by about 1e-6 mm. Its vertices then sit on alternate sides of the move. The check reads this as a crossing, and the wall check excuses the move.

## Expected

A crossing needs each neighbour off the trace line by at least a small distance, for example `CROSSING_TOUCH`. A neighbour nearer than that counts as on the line, and the move answers to the walls as before.

## Also

The arc branch of `Trace::through` (`crates/sim/src/verify/arc_wall.rs`) has no direct pin.

## Done means

- A pin for a wall along the trace with a wobble below the band. The move still answers to the walls.
- A pin for a true crossing with neighbours beyond the band. The move crosses.
- A pin for the arc branch of `Trace::through`.

title: Bore with entry Ramp and no ramp angle descends on a steep chord (up to 84 deg) at the cutting feed

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3

body:
Found by a probe after PR #1663 (#1609). Upstream main 2b6e03f2.

**What happens.** A Bore with `entry: Ramp` and no ramp angle ramps at each level on a chord. The chord goes from the previous ring start to the centre, so it is only as long as the ring radius. The chord angle increases when the hole becomes smaller. All of these chords are at the cutting feed, with no note:

| Hole | Steepest chord into material |
|---|---|
| Ø16 | 21.8° |
| Ø12 | 33.7° |
| Ø8 | 63.4° |
| Ø7 | 84.3° |

Each ring also starts again with a `Plunge` move at the plunge feed and no note, although Ramp is the selected entry.

**Repro.** Bore, one blind hole Ø7 at (0,0). Top 0, floor -6, tool diameter 6, corner radius 0, stepdown 2, `entry: Ramp`, links `PLANAR`, feed 500, plunge feed 250. The path has `Feed (0.2,0,0) -> (0,0,-2)`, a chord of 84° at 500 with no note, at each level.

**Expected.** As #1609 and #1663 do for a Circular, a ramp entry descends at no more than the ramp angle. If it cannot, it substitutes by name: a plunge at the plunge feed with an `entry:` note. The `Plunge` that starts each ring again also gets a note.

**Done means:** a pin on the repro (and on Ø12) shows that every descending feed move is at most the ramp angle, or is a named plunge at the plunge feed. The pin is red on today's code and is mutation-checked.

body:
Found by a probe after PR #1663 (#1609). Upstream main 2b6e03f2.

**What happens.** A 2D Contour with side Inside and `entry: Ramp` feeds straight down into the material at the cutting feed at each level. The path has no note. The cause is in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour_bore.rs`, in the `Entry3D::Ramp =>` arm (near line 111). The chord goes from the leg to the ring start. On a closed ring, these are the same point, so the chord has no length. The code checks only the center cut (`contour_link::guard`). Then it pushes a `Feed` to `e2` at the cutting feed. This code does not use `descent::plan_arm`, so the fix of #1663 does not apply to it.

**Repro.** `contour` on a square, half-width 20 at the origin. Tool diameter 6, side Inside, `lead: Lead::None`, top 0, bottom -6, stepdown 2, `entry: Ramp`, `blend_turns: false`, links `PLANAR`, retract 2, feed 500, plunge feed 250. The path has `Feed (-17,-17,0) -> (-17,-17,-2)` at 500 with no note. The levels -2 to -4 and -4 to -6 are the same.

A Contour with side Outside is correct. It makes named axial plunges at the plunge feed.

**Expected.** A ramp entry descends at no more than the ramp angle, for example as a zig-zag along the ring. If it cannot, it substitutes by name: a plunge at the plunge feed with an `entry:` note. A straight-down feed at the cutting feed with no note is never correct.

**Done means:** a pin on the repro shows that every descending feed move is at most the ramp angle, or is a named plunge at the plunge feed. The pin is red on today's code and is mutation-checked.

title: Face: last pass tangent to the stock edge gets a false Gouge with a 4 mm mill

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## Problem

A stock-source Face with the catalog mill `EM-0400-2FL` (diameter 4 mm) gets a `Gouge` warning on its last pass when that pass is tangent to the stock edge. The post then refuses the program. The document has no part. The pass is above the stock top. Thus no material is in the way, and the warning looks like a false positive.

## How to see it

Found while working on #1657 (a scratch probe in `crates/app/tests/`, not committed):

1. Make a new world with no part.
2. Add the tool `EM-0400-2FL`.
3. Set a stock `StockShape::Box { dx: 64, dy: 64, dz: 32 }` at `pos (30, 30, 0)`. The stock is x and y -2..62, z 0..32.
4. Create a Face on `SrcRef::Stock`: `stepover 3`, `cut_z 34`, `clearance_z 45`.
5. Generate it.

The result:

- The passes run at y = 0, 3, ..., 60, x -4..64.
- Move 42 (the last pass, `(-4, 60, 34) -> (64, 60, 34)`) gets `Gouge`.
- The tool edge at y = 60 touches y = 62, the stock edge, exactly.

Other readings:

- `dy 65`, `66` or `70`: no warning.
- `EM-0600-4FL` and `EM-1000-4FL` with `dy 64`: no warning.
- `cut_z 30.5`, `31.5`, `34` and stepovers 3, 2.9, 1.5: the same `Gouge`.
- The first pass at y = 0 is also 2 mm from the stock edge (y = -2), but it gets no warning.

A likely place is the section law `tangency` in `crates/sim/src/verify/section.rs` (`d(center, boundary) >= r - leave - tol` against the region loops). This is not confirmed.

I did not check if this occurs before the merges of PR 1622, PR 1634, PR 1640 and PR 1644. The probe has no part, so the keep law of #1607 is not the cause.

## Done means

The Face above posts without a warning, or the warning is shown to be correct with a reason. A test in the crate that owns the judgement pins the result. A true gouge near the stock edge is still refused.

The post-merge gate on main `1bd9298d6b1b5bb2858de6388f9b4d2691023249` is red (run 43587095462). Two suites failed.

**Failure 1 - a real regression: the ui suites.**
Test: `egui_app::tests::setup_mount_pages::each_setup_picks_its_own_machine_and_post_and_posts_one_file_per_mount`
The test panics at `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_mount_pages.rs:101`. The post is refused. The message says:

> post blocked - Setup1 (VMC 3-AXIS, Fanuc (built-in)): 18 warning(s): Face1: rapid move 0 travels below the clearance plane inside stock; Face1: move 19 cuts past the finish surface; ... (17 more move warnings)

Nothing wrong was posted - the refusal worked. The gouge check now judges this fixture toolpath as unsafe.

**The cause is in the merge range `53a77c9dc..1bd9298d6`.**
The ui suites passed on `7c07e86830880fde86a575d86d34ff9fb89afd07` (run 43584872633). Only four merges landed between the two heads: #1622, #1634, #1640, #1644. All four change how a 2D cut is judged against the parts. One of them makes the check fire on this toolpath now.

Test: `a_lowered_cap_refuses_the_same_face_at_once` failed at `crates/app/tests/import_step_guard.rs:36` with "import did not finish within 30s". The fix for #1605 merged at `141bc0696` (PR #1652). It moves that test to its own binary. No work is owed for this part.

title: 2D Adaptive on a model source skips an outside band narrower than the tool with no note

labels.name: bug

labels.name: area:2d

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Part of #1554 (the second finding of that issue). The fix for #1554 changes only the stock source. This issue holds the model-source case.

## What happens

A 2D Adaptive with the model as the source clears the stock around the part (#12). When the stock margin is narrower than the tool, the outside band is dropped. The op comes back `ok` with no note and no warning. The outside of the part is not cut.

Reading from #1554: a 3.175 mm margin per side with a 6 mm tool. All 51,188 feed points are inside the bore. A pick of the band is refused with `pocket is narrower than the tool`.

## Cause (first reading)

`machining2d::pocket_entered` erodes the region by the tool radius. A region piece that erodes to nothing gets no pass. Only an empty result in total is refused. A dropped piece gets no note.

## Expected

One of these:
- The op cuts the outside band. The band is open to air on its outer side, so the tool can hang over the stock edge.
- The op carries a note that names the skipped band and the cause.

## Risk

A note in the generator can change the CL notes of existing pockets that leave narrow slivers. Check the goldens before a change.

Done means: a model-source adaptive with a stock margin narrower than the tool cuts the band, or carries a note that names the skipped band. A test pins it.

body:
The maintainer reported this in chat on 2026-11-14:

> on the WCS page - under Quarter turns - there should be a "flip X", "flip Y" and "flip Z" button.. and what that does is flipping X+ to X- direction and vice versa for the other direction - without turning the gizmo around nother axis. As some machine has their directions reversed...

Expected: three buttons, `Flip X`, `Flip Y` and `Flip Z`, are below Quarter turns on the WCS page. Each button reverses the direction of one WCS axis. The other two axes do not move.

Open design points:
- A flip of one axis makes a left-handed frame. A rotation quaternion cannot store it. The WCS needs a sign for each axis, or an equivalent record, in the project file.
- A flip changes the sign of posted coordinates on that axis. It also changes arc direction (`G2`/`G3`), cutter compensation side (`G41`/`G42`) and the climb or conventional sense. The post must write these correctly, or refuse the program with a named reason.
- Simulation and the gouge checks must use the same frame as the post.
- The gizmo must show the flipped axis.

Each flip is an undoable command. It ships with an MCP tool, or a follow-up `MCP:` issue names it.

Effort is `effort:high` because the change can alter posted G-code (safety floor).

Done means: the three buttons are on the WCS page, each flip is one undo step, the project file keeps the flips, and golden NC tests pin the posted output of a flipped axis, with arcs and cutter compensation.

title: A part-source cross drill is not judged against the setup's other parts (#1621's neighbour law skips it)

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while fixing #1635 (PR #1640). I read this from the code and have not reproduced it with a run.

**What happens.** #1621 judges a part-source operation against the setup's OTHER parts (`keep_law::neighbour_parts`). It does so only for kinds that carry a part law, i.e. `depth_law_of(params, src, true)` is not `None`. A Drill with cross holes reads `DepthLaw::None`, so `neighbour_parts` is empty for it. Its chain answers only to `cross_part` against its own source's mesh, and since #1640 also against the setup's parts when the source is the stock.

So a cross hole drilled on part B, from a raw stock that also holds part A, whose drill or approach enters A, may carry no finding on the op. The program sim refuses to judge a posed (radial) chain, so whether such a program then posts is the open question.

**Expected.** A part-source cross drill that enters a neighbouring part is a blocking finding on the op, or is refused by name.

Done means:
- a test with a part-source cross drill on B entering a neighbouring part A is refused or blocked;
- the same drill clear of A still posts.

Part of the #1621 / #1635 part laws.

title: An op judged against parts beside its source does not read Stale when one of them moves

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d

labels.name: area:sim

labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happens:** since #1603 (stock-source pocket family), #1607 (every stock-source 2D kind with a part law) and #1621 (a part-source op against the setup's other parts, PR #1622), an operation's verdict is read against parts BESIDE its source (`keep_law::parts_in_stock`, `keep_law::neighbour_parts`). The op's stamp (`operation::stamp::current_stamp`) still digests only the source (plus the stock for a non-stock source). So after a clean generation, a part that is moved into the cut, added, un-tagged as a fixture, or un-marked as raw stock only leaves the op `Ok` with a verdict nobody gave.

- Aligned stock: the program sim judges every part live at post and refuses.
- **Turned stock** (the sim refuses to judge): the post reads the ops' cached verdicts - all `Ok` and clean - and the program goes out into the moved part. Same hole the original #1603 / #1607 / #1621 fixes closed, re-opened by an edit after generation.

The other direction is fail-safe but confusing: marking a casting raw stock only (#1094) or moving a neighbour away leaves the op `Ok` with its old gouges cached; the post refuses until the user regenerates for no visible reason.

**Tried on PR #1622 and pulled back** (branch `issue/1607-stock-source-law`: f4d86b41 and 6abccc77 add it, the commit after dae97790 takes it out again): a stamp term digesting the kept set (`name`, `setup_align::pose_in`, `model::geometry_signature` of each model the part laws read; written only when the set is non-empty). It works (pinned: moving the neighbour makes the op Stale; red without the term), but it breaks established stamp contracts that need a maintainer's call:
- `fixtures.rs::workholding_never_stales_a_fresh_toolpath` - un-tagging a vise turns it into a part, so the op goes Stale (the "workholding never stales" law, M2.3).
- `operations.rs::a_frommodel_stock_survives_its_source_being_deleted` and `a_model_update_does_not_touch_a_box_stock` - "a stock-based path never reads the model": a stock-source Face now does (its parts).
- `fidelity_copies.rs` (2 tests) - deleting the stock's coarse source model makes the stock-source op Stale, so the gate says "regenerate" instead of the named fidelity refusal.
- `stock_source_verdict.rs` - marking the casting raw stock only stales a part-source op.

**Options:** (a) the stamp term above, restating those contracts (the kept parts are inputs; workholding stays out only while it is tagged); (b) no stamp term, but the post re-reads the part laws live for ops whose kept set changed (like the workholding gate does), so nothing churns; (c) (b) only when the sim cannot judge.

Found while fixing #1621 (PR #1622; `docs/decisions/1607-stock-source-law.md`).

Done means: a part moved into a stock-source or part-source op's cut after generation never posts on a turned stock (refused by name, Stale or live re-judgement); the chosen option's contract changes are decided and recorded; pinned and mutation-checked.

What happens: the "Clippy on the touched crates" step of `pr-test.yml` fails on the self-hosted runner for any PR that touches `camcraft-geometry`, with three `needless_range_loop` errors ("loop variable `slot` is only used to index `e.facets`") in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/feature.rs` at lines 481, 1205 and 1486. The lines are not part of the PR that hit it.

Evidence:
- Run 43546645706 (PR 1576, head `e7d78efe`, runner `uma`): clippy step red with the three errors above. The log's help links point at `rust-1.100.0`.
- Main at `c00ba18a9`, local Windows machine, rustc 1.99.0 / clippy 0.1.99: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings` exits 0 with no lints.

Not verified: that the three lines are byte-identical on main and on PR 1576's head (the PR's reviewer read them as untouched by the PR).

Expected: the same clippy verdict on the runner and locally, and a green clippy step for a PR that did not touch the flagged lines.

- Rewrite the three loops as iterator loops (`for (slot, f) in e.facets.iter().enumerate()` or the form clippy suggests), with no behaviour change. This is geometry code, so the change is read with care and the feature suites run.
- Decide whether the toolchain is pinned (a `rust-toolchain.toml` is a file `pr-test.yml` refuses in a PR diff, so that part is the maintainer's decision).

Done means: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on clippy 1.100 and 1.99, and the clippy step of a `pr-test.yml` run on a geometry-touching PR is green.

title: STEP import: a closed, gap-free solid wound inward imports inside out (signed volume < 0), nothing says so

labels.name: bug

body:
What happens: a STEP solid whose faces are all wound inward (consistently, so no face disagrees with a neighbour) imports with a negative signed volume. Nothing flips it and nothing says so. Seen with the local older test part `step-block-371.step` (20 facets, V = -102000 mm^3) on upstream main and on the #1576 branch alike, found in the review of PR #1576 (issue #1573). A synthetic stand-in reproduces it: `testdata/models/box.step` with every `same_sense` (FACE_SURFACE and FACE_BOUND) inverted imports with V = -1, `notes = []`.

Why #1576 leaves it: its rule flips faces only where neighbours disagree, so a consistently inverted shell is untouched. Deciding "outward" when nothing flipped is wrong for an open or lone-face shell (a curved open face's centroid volume has no meaning), so it needs a guard: closed, gap-free (the seams judge already knows) and every shared edge opposite.

What a wrong winding can do, as far as traced:
- `crates/app/src/pick/winding.rs` already refuses face picks on a wound-inward body by name, so alignment to it is refused, not wrong.
- The solid law (`crates/sim/src/verify/solid.rs`) reads the mesh by ray parity, which does not depend on winding, so the gouge check is not fooled on this evidence.
- NOT traced: generators or checks that read facet normals directly (3D finishing, pocket3d offsets, tool-side). Whoever works this should grep them and test one op on an inverted box; if any gouges or cuts the wrong side, raise to P1.

Rating: P3 (wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround: re-export or import an STL; the picks refuse). By the AGENTS.md safety floor the fix touches geometry, so effort:high.

Done means: a closed, gap-free STEP shell with every shared edge opposite and a negative signed volume is flipped outward at import and says so in the import notes (the `Graded`/MCP `notes` and status line); an open or lone-face shell is left alone; pinning tests for the inverted box and for the lone-curved-face case; the unchecked normal-reading ops listed above are checked against an inverted box and the result is commented here.

**Same pattern elsewhere** (from the synth goldens, `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/synth_*.nc`):
- `grblhal.cps`, `carvera.cps`: `T2 M6` ... `G0 X20 Y10` is a bare X/Y traverse at whatever height the tool change left, then `G0 X20 Y10 Z-3`. This is exactly the #1614 shape.
- `fanuc.cps`, `haas.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `sinumerik.cps`, `heidenhain.cps`: after `G43 H..`, the first block is the stream's first rapid as one combined move, `G00 X20 Y10 Z-3`. It goes in a straight line from the tool-change height. It is safe only while that start height is above the part. With a tool too long for the work offset, the line starts below the part top.
- `tinyg.cps`: check it too (it lifts with `G53 G0 Z0` after `M0`, then traverses).

**Done means:** each spindle mill post states the section's clearance Z (a Z-only rapid to `ClearancePlane`, else `RetractPlane`) before its first X/Y motion after a tool change and at the program start. A stream stating neither is refused by name. There is a pinning test per post. Moved goldens are regenerated and listed in the PR (expect one added `G0 Z` line per program, as #1614 saw across 32 Tormach goldens).

Part of the #1614 follow-up.

title: Tormach post: the first XY traverse after a tool change rides at the top of Z even when that is below the part's clearance (Hub: down, over, up)

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**Found in a PathPilot Hub run (770MX sim, v2.14.4, 2026-11-13)** of the merged #1357 golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/drill_peck.nc`, posted inch for the 770MX.

**What happened.** In Hub's tool table T4 is 5.0000" long. With the session's G54 Z zero, the top of Z travel was only about 4.3" above work Z0. The program runs:

```
G53 G0 Z0        (top of travel)
G30
T4 M6
G43 H4           (5" tool: the tip is now about 0.68" BELOW work Z0, though nothing moved)
S1500 M3
M8
G0 X0.7874 Y0.3937       <- the XY traverse at that height: below the part top
G0 X0.7874 Y0.3937 Z0    <- then UP to Z0
```

The user saw the tool go down, then over, then up. "Down" is the 5" length offset taking effect. "Over" is the XY rapid with the tip about 0.68" below the stock surface. "Up" is the rapid to Z0. On a real machine that traverse would drive the tool through the part or the vise. At load time PathPilot warned "Program exceeds machine maximum on Z axis by 0.5107 in (line 0)", but the post still writes a traverse that cannot clear.

**Cause.** `tormach.cps` (`xyFirst` / `startXY`) makes the first XY move after a tool change "at the current - safe, Z-up - height". It assumes the top of travel is above the part. It never states the section's clearance Z before the traverse. When the tool is too long for the work offset, the top of travel is below that clearance.

**Proposed fix.** After `G43 H..`, and before the first XY traverse, write `G0 Z<clearance>` from the section's `ClearancePlane` (or its first rapid's Z). On a setup that can clear, this is an ordinary move down to clearance. On a setup that cannot, the control refuses the block as beyond its Z limit and stops. That is a visible refusal, not a rapid through the part. Pin it with a test: a stream whose first XY rapid follows a tool change shows `G0 Z<clearance>` before it. Regenerate the Tormach goldens this moves (listed in the PR). Check whether the other mill posts share the assumption, and file each one that does.

**Done means:** no Tormach program makes its first XY traverse after a tool change without first stating the clearance Z. That is pinned by a test, and the moved goldens are listed in the PR.

Related: #1357 (merged), the Hub session screenshots of 2026-11-13 17:55.

title: Stock-source Engrave, Trace and the typed 2D kinds cut the part with no op finding and post on a turned stock

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
**What happens:** a 2D operation whose source is the **stock** (or a pick off the setup's stock) carries no part law on the operation (`part_solid` is false, so `depth_law_of` returns `DepthLaw::None` before the kind's arm). When the stock holds a part and the cut reaches into it, the operation has 0 findings. With the stock aligned the program sim blocks the post; with the stock **turned** (the sim refuses to judge) the post goes out.

Found while working #1595 / #1603 (branch `issue/1595-engrave-law`, upstream main 745edc36 plus that branch).

**Probe:** the #1585 fixture (40 x 40 x 8 block, R15 pocket to Z4, EM-0600-4FL) in a 40 x 40 x 8 box stock centred over it. Engrave / Trace, source `Stock`, Top Z8, Bottom Z1 (the stock's outline is the part's outline, so the line runs down the part's outside wall):

| kind | op findings | stock aligned | stock turned 90 deg about Z |
|---|---|---|---|
| Engrave | 0 | blocked by the program sim ("worst 7.00 mm") | **posts** |
| Trace | 0 | blocked by the program sim ("worst 7.00 mm") | **posts** |

The same holds by construction for the other kinds that are judged only on a part source: Slot, Trochoidal slot, Circular (`authored_law`), Contour and Face (`Section`). #1593 pinned the stock-source Trochoidal slot as never judged (`a_trochoid_on_the_stock_is_never_judged`); these were not probed here.

**What #1603's fix covers and what it leaves:** the pocket family (2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset) on a stock source is now judged against the setup's parts (`operation::keep_law::parts_in_stock`, the mesh the program sim judges against). The job carries those parts only for that family. Every other kind on a stock source is still unjudged on the operation.

**Expected:** a stock-source operation in a setup that holds a part is judged against that part by the law its kind takes on a part source (Mark for Engrave / Trace, with the sim's mark credit extended to match; Section for the typed kinds, Contour and Face), or the decision that the stock source is never judged is restated with a refusal where the program sim cannot judge. Either way the aligned and the turned stock give the same verdict.

**Not simply `uncovered()`:** refusing every None-law op when the sim cannot judge would refuse a legal stock-source Face on any turned stock (see `docs/decisions/1595-engrave-mark-law.md`).

**Done means:** the probe rows above are refused on the operation by name (or the post is blocked) on both stocks; a legal stock-source cut that stays off the part (a Face above it, a Contour round the stock) still posts on both; `a_trochoid_on_the_stock_is_never_judged` is kept or replaced by a stated decision; pinned through generate and the post, mutation-checked.

Related: #1603, #1595, #1593, #1554.

body:
**What happens:** whole-model 2D Pocket and 2D Adaptive (and the stock-source Adaptive of #1554) can cut into the part with **no finding on the op**. On a **turned (rotated) stock** the post goes out, because the program sim refuses to judge a turned stock and nothing else catches it. Found by M5's review of PR #1597 (pullrequestreview-5899991928), on upstream main be27a4c7 plus #1597.

| Case | Depth into the part | Op findings | Aligned stock | Turned stock |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pocket / Adaptive2D, whole-model source, Area offset +3 | 4.0-4.25 mm | 0 | blocked by the program sim | **posts** |
| Pocket / Adaptive2D, whole-model source, extension +5 | 5 mm | 0 | blocked by the program sim | **posts** |
| #1554: stock-source Adaptive2D / Pocket | 7 mm | 0 | blocked by the program sim | **posts** |

With default area controls (and containment On or Outside) these ops stay outside the part (worst clearance -0.005 mm). The gouge needs a positive area offset or extension, or a stock source.

**Why:** these ops carry `DepthLaw::None`, so the op itself never judges the cut against the model. `uncovered()` (crates/app/src/posting_sim.rs) counts any fresh, stamped op as judged whatever its depth law, so when the program sim cannot model the stock (turned, posed, rotary), a None-law op that cuts the part goes to the post. Same root as #1595 (Engrave/Trace) and the TrochoidalSlot gap fixed by #1597. This is a gouge that passes on a turned stock: P1.

**Expected:** a whole-model or stock-source Pocket or Adaptive2D whose cut reaches into the part is refused on the op by name (a law that judges the region it actually cuts against the model), or at minimum `uncovered()` refuses to post a None-law op on a model source when the program sim cannot judge it. Legal whole-model pockets with default controls must still post. That is why #1597 did not simply make `uncovered()` refuse every None-law op.

**Done means:** the three rows above are refused (on the op, and the post is blocked) with the stock aligned and turned; legal whole-model pockets and adaptives with default controls still post on both. Pinned through `operation::generate` and the post, mutation-checked.

Related: #1595 (the same `uncovered()` question for Engrave/Trace), #1554 (stock-source Adaptive: not only verify-caught; it posts on a turned stock), #1593 / PR #1597, #1550.

title: STEP import: two AP214 parts of mostly cylinders and cones run 10 min and 2 GB, then refuse or never finish

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
## What happens

Two AP214 part files from the user (`10208.STEP`, `32050.STEP`; not attached — they are the user's, available on request) do not import, on the head of PR #1576 (bda36c6e, which carries #1574 and #1573's closed-shell check), debug `camcraft-cli script` → `cam.import`:

| File | Faces | Surfaces | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `10208.STEP` | 67 in 2 `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` / `CLOSED_SHELL` | 31 cylinder, 12 cone, 19 plane, 2 sphere, 3 rational B-spline | **refused after 588 s, 2.3 GB RSS**: `closed shell #1319 (52 faces) meshes open: 13227 unmatched edges, the first from (4.8174, 4.1370, -6.7542) to (5.1105, 3.7690, -6.7776) mm` |
| `32050.STEP` | 101 in 2 solids | 52 cylinder, 13 cone, 33 plane, 3 rational B-spline | **killed by a 600 s timeout, 2.2 GB RSS**: no result (a hang to the user) |

For comparison `sc_logo.step` (#1536) imports in 1.5 s on the same build.

## Why it is P1

A user-triggered import that runs 10 minutes and 2 GB without an end is the #1536 failure class ("never finishes"). And 13,227 unmatched edges on a 52-face shell of mostly cylinders and cones from a CAD export says the importer meshes these faces wrongly, not that the file is corrupt; #1576's refusal is the safety net doing its job, but it tells the user to re-export a file that is very likely fine.

## Where to look

- The meter from #1546 and the pass-wide budget idea in #1599 bound the time but not the cause.
- The 3 rational B-spline faces per file (`BOUNDED_SURFACE ... RATIONAL_B_SPLINE_SURFACE`) are the likely runaway; the analytic faces should mesh in milliseconds. First step: time each face's tessellation and find which face eats the budget and which faces own the unmatched edges.

## Done means

Both files import closed in seconds (or one names the face it cannot mesh within a bounded time, never minutes), with a fixture that reproduces the runaway (a rebuilt face, not the user's file), pinned by a test.

Found while checking #1574/#1576 against the user's files.

**What happens:** Engrave and Trace fall to `DepthLaw::None` in `depth_law_of` (crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs) for every source ("they enter the part by design"). Found while auditing the 2D kinds for #1593 (upstream main 7bfb1824 + the #1593 fix).

- Both follow every model edge - the R15 pocket ring and the block outline - down to Z1: 516 moves below Z3.9, at radius 15.00..28.28. That is 3 mm under the pocket floor and 7 mm down the outside wall.
- **Stock aligned:** op findings 0; the post is blocked only by the program sim ("gouge: program cuts below the model in 1771 cell(s), worst 7.00 mm at (-19.94, -19.94, z 1.00)").
- **Stock turned 90 deg about Z** (same footprint; the program sim refuses to judge it): op findings 0, and **the post goes out**. `uncovered()` (posting_sim.rs) counts any fresh, stamped op as judged whatever its depth law.

**Expected:** an Engrave or Trace on the finished part has a depth law the op itself carries, so the verdict does not depend on whether the program sim can model the stock: a cut deeper than the engraving/trace contract allows is a named gouge on the op and holds the post; a legal engraving posts on both stocks.

Engrave/Trace cut the part on purpose, so `Section` would convict every legal engraving; this needs its own law (e.g. a depth budget below the traced edge, or refuse on a model source when the program sim cannot judge). body:
**Request (the user, from a PathPilot Hub run of PR #1577's kit, 2026-11-13):** they saw the program end go up and then come back down. Asked how a program should end, they chose to drop the `G53 G0 Z0` and keep `G30`, and in their words: "I would expect there to be a G0 A0. (if there is a 4th axis) --- but the G53 G0 Z0 perhaps should not be there".

**Today** (`assets/posts/tormach.cps`, `retract()` and `onClose()`): the program ends `M9`, `M5`, `G53 G0 Z0`, `G30`, `M30`. In the Hub the `G53 G0 Z0` lifted to the top of travel, then `G30` brought Z back down to the sim's stored G30 position (machine Z -1.5611), which looks like the tool dropping back toward the part.

**Asked for:**
1. End the program with `G30` (the operator's preset G30 / unload position) and no `G53 G0 Z0` before it.
2. On a machine with a 4th axis, return the rotary with `G0 A0` at the end.

**Safety:** this changes posted G-code and is under the safety floor, so it needs a safety-tier review. The current order is deliberate.
- The post's own comments (#495, #785, PR #798) note that a G30 with no axis words moves EVERY axis to the stored position (LinuxCNC params 5181-5189), X, Y and A included, so Z goes straight up first.
- Without the lift, a G30 whose stored position includes X/Y, or a Z below the part top, rapids there **from the last cutting height** and could cross the part or the vise.
- The design must keep the end safe whatever the operator's G30 holds. Options:
  - drop the lift only when the machine file states the G30 position is Z-only and above the part;
  - keep a lift to a clearance height in work coordinates (above the stock) instead of machine Z0;
  - make the ending a post option, with today's order as the default.
- The worker records the chosen option and why in `docs/decisions/`.
- **Where `G0 A0` goes:** after Z is clear of the part, never before.

**Done means:**
- The Tormach program end follows the request, or a safe variant of it, with the reasoning in the decision file.
- A machine with a 4th axis ends with `G0 A0` after the tool is clear.
- The affected Tormach NC goldens are regenerated and explained.
- A pin shows no end move rapids X/Y below the clearance height.
- The PathPilot Hub kit runs to M30 on the 770MX sim.

Related: #495, #785, PR #798, PR #1577 (whose Hub run surfaced this).

body:
**What happens:** the stand-alone **Trochoidal slot** operation cuts endpoints and a width that the user types by hand, but its depth law falls to `DepthLaw::None`. Nothing on the op judges whether it cuts into the model. Found by M5's review of PR #1585 (pullrequestreview-5899641890), on upstream main 45a76e15 plus #1585.

With a whole-model (Entity) source:
- **3 mm below a pocket floor:** generate says ok with no findings. With the stock **rotated** (the program sim refuses to judge), the post goes out. With the stock aligned, the program sim blocks it.
- **Through the pocket wall to Z4:** generate says ok with no findings, and it **posts with the stock aligned as well as rotated**. The program sim misses it too.

That second case is a gouge that passes every check: P1 under AGENTS.md.

**Why:** `depth_law_of` (crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs) has no arm that gives Trochoidal slot a judging law. #1564/#1585 added `authored_law` for Circular and Slot only. `uncovered()` in posting_sim.rs counts any fresh, stamped op as judged whatever its depth law.

**Expected:** a Trochoidal slot with an Entity or Selection source is judged against the model like the Slot (`authored_law`: Entity/Selection → Section, Stock → None), so both cases above refuse at the op and at the post.

**Done means:** both repros above (below the floor, and through the wall, each with aligned and rotated stock) are refused with a named gouge on the op, and the post is blocked. Pins go through `operation::generate` and the post. Mutating the Trochoidal-slot arm to `None` turns them red. Also consider whether `uncovered()` should refuse an op whose depth law is `None` while its source is the model, so the next op type cannot fall through the same way.

Related: #1503 (closed, the earlier trochoidal-slot cut into the model), #1523 (one slot confine law), #1590 (the op's future), #1550 / PR #1585, #1543.

title: Trochoidal slot leaves a post at its start when the loop band is wider than the tool

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while working #1509.

What happens: the stand-alone Trochoidal slot bores its entry helix on a circle of the loop band's half-width `b = (W - D) / 2 - leave` about the centre line's start (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/trochoid_bore.rs`, the plain bore; before #1509's PR the same code in `trochoid_slot.rs`, `emit_level`). A helix of radius `b` clears the ring `b +- r`. With `b > r` (a slot wider than twice the tool: W > 2 D) a post of radius `b - r` is left standing at the bore's centre, full depth. No front arc reaches it (the loops only advance away from the bore), the operation reports OK, and the verifier has nothing to say (uncut material is not a gouge).

Evidence: on a band of half-width 4.9 mm with a 6 mm tool (post radius 1.9 mm), the plain bore leaves more than 4 mm2 standing inside a 1.4 mm disc about the start, read on the dexel stock (`quality::rest_area`); the test `the_opened_bore_leaves_no_post_at_the_lane_start` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive_troch_tests.rs` asserts it for the plain bore and its absence for the opened one. The maintainer's #1503 screenshot (W 16, D 6: b = 5, r = 3) has a 2 mm radius post at A.

Expected: no post. The 2D Adaptive trochoidal method already opens its bore (`trochoid_bore::bore` with `open: true`: helix at half the tool radius, then a two-centre semicircle spiral out to the band, read by the same engagement measurement). The stand-alone slot can take the same bore; that moves its output for W > 2 D (its golden `trochoid_slot_small.cl` has b < r and does not move).

Done means: a Trochoidal slot with W > 2 D leaves no standing material inside its channel at the start (a rest reading in the motion suite), the engagement limit still holds, and slots with b <= r post byte-identically.

body:
**What happens.** The carried-workholding check (`app::fixture_carried`, the carried dexel body against a fixture) knows the carried part only at its grid's column centres. At a side face or a step of the carried part, a fixture's steel that reaches into the material by less than one grid pitch, and stops short of the next material column centre, is not refused.

This is not new with PR #1549: main's box law (`penetration`) has the same blind band. The M3 review of PR #1549 measured it (pullrequestreview-5898992751):
- A single box jaw overlapping a part's side face by 0.9 pitch, at 11 phases against the grid: main and the PR agree at every phase (10 refusals, 1 pass where a column centre lies exactly on the jaw face).
- The flipped hat at pitch 0.375: a jaw overlapping by 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.7 pitch passes on main and on the PR; at 0.9 pitch and more both refuse (`5.00 mm deep`).

**Bound.** By construction under one pitch: steel more than one pitch inside a face covers a material column's lines or lies in a rectangle of four material columns, which PR #1549 reads whole. On the shipped grid (`max(r/8, span/1023)`) that is 0.375 mm on the test stock, about 1 mm on 1 m stock.

**Expected.** Side-face contact resolved finer than one pitch (for example, reading the carried part's own side faces, or a finer local grid where a fixture face lies within a cell of a material boundary), or the bound stated in the refusal law and pinned.

**Done means:** side-face contact is resolved finer than one pitch, or the bound is pinned at several phases of the face against the grid (main's and the mesh reading's verdicts asserted equal, and the passing depth asserted below one pitch).

Refs #1530. Found in the review of PR #1549 (https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/1549).

title: 2D Contour arc fit at a coarse tolerance sits 0.01 mm past the wall on a tessellated cylinder (verify holds it as a gouge), depending on walk direction

labels.name: bug

labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while fixing #1555 (PR #1577).

**What happens.** `crates/ui/src/law_tests.rs::arc_moves_draw_curved` builds a 2D Contour around a Ø30 cylinder stock (`SrcRef::Stock`, Side Auto, EM-0400-2FL, tolerance 0.1). Walked clockwise (climb after #1555), `fit_arcs` fits three arcs about centre (-0.0034, 0.0034) with radius about 16.995, so the arcs dip about 0.010 mm inside the tool-radius offset. `verify` reports `Gouge` at every arc move (`[Gouge { at: 3 }, { at: 4 }, { at: 5 }, ...]`) and the post is held, so this is not silent. Walked counter-clockwise, the same ring fits two arcs plus two lines and passes, by luck of where the fitter splits. The fitter walks each ring from its own end, so the split points, and so the sag past the wall, depend on direction.

**Expected.** At any tolerance the user picks, the fitted contour does not cross the offset by more than the verify's gouge tolerance. Either the fit is one-sided (sag only into air) or the fitter re-splits an arc that dips past the offset. It should never produce a path the gate then refuses as a gouge.

**Workaround.** A finer tolerance (0.01) on the operation.

**Evidence.** On PR #1577's branch, set `climb: true` in `arc_moves_draw_curved` (that PR pins it on `climb: false` for now) and print `cache.warnings`.

Done means: a contour fitted at tolerance 0.1 on a tessellated round wall verifies clean in both walk directions, pinned by a test that runs both, and `arc_moves_draw_curved` goes back to the climb walk.

title: STEP import: a closed shell whose mesh is not closed imports silently (faces dropped or mis-trimmed by truck pass as a model)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while fixing #1548 (PR to follow).

**What happens.** The STEP importer keeps whatever truck's tessellation returns for a shell. Two things can go wrong inside truck without any error reaching us, and both leave a mesh with holes that imports as a normal model:

- A face whose boundary cannot be placed on its surface gets no polygon (`None`). `to_polygon()` skips it (`truck-meshalgo` `tessellation/mod.rs`, `MeshedShape for CompressedShell<.., Option<PolygonMesh>>`), and `shell_facets` (`crates/app/src/geometry/import/step.rs`) never looks.
- A face whose boundary is placed wrongly is trimmed wrongly and loses triangles.

The file says `CLOSED_SHELL` / `MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP`, the mesh is open, and nothing is refused or flagged (`coarse_mm` is `None`). The stock simulation and every verdict then judge the program against a model with missing walls. That is the Prime Directive's worst case: a silent wrong answer.

**Evidence** (measured on the #1548 branch base, d569372f, with a debug build):

- A 30 mm cube with all 12 edges rounded R3.125, written by solidcore's step-export: imported with no refusal at **14,993 mm3 of 26,286** (57%), 86 unmatched edges. Every planar face had lost a corner and the cylinders part of their area. (#1548 fixes the two causes found on that file; the importer still has no check that would have caught it.)
- After #1548, variants of `testdata/models/fillet_corner.step` with the corner blend bent (weights `1E300, 1E-300`; a knot at `1.0E300`; a zero-length knot span) import with the blend face dropped: 138 facets, open, no refusal. See `import_step_corner_blend::bent_corner_blends_end_cleanly_and_bounded`, which only asserts "bounded and finite" today.

**Expected.** A shell the file declares closed must mesh closed, or the import is refused by name (which shell, how many unmatched edges, where the first one is), the same way #1536 refuses a face that never converges. A face truck returns no polygon for is refused by name on its own. An `OPEN_SHELL` / surface model is out of scope: it may be open.

**Notes.**
- Welding: adjacent faces evaluate a shared boundary point on their own surfaces, so the copies differ by up to about 1e-7; near a patch pole two copies of the vertex differ by about 4e-9 and leave a sliver facet with two welded corners. The test helper `open_edges` in `crates/app/tests/import_step_corner_blend.rs` welds by neighbourhood at 1e-6 and skips collapsed facets; all existing STEP fixtures (`box`, `bspline_dome`, `Milling-test`, `Milling-test-inch`, `sample_ap214`, `lathe_holder_offset`, `empty_list`, `tool_csys_box_iso13399`) measure 0 unmatched edges with it, so the law should not refuse any of them.
- Observation for triage, not verified as a defect of ours: the files solidcore's `step-export` wrote from a bare `brep_to_model` had every face sense inward, and they import with a negative volume and no message. Whether a STEP solid with inward senses should be refused, flipped or flagged is a separate question.

**Done means:** a STEP whose closed shell meshes open is refused by name inside the normal import time, pinned by a fixture with one face truck cannot place (for example a bent variant of `fillet_corner.step`) and by a test that every existing STEP fixture still imports. Each new refusal has a test that fails when its line is deleted.

Related: #1536, #1545, #1548.

title: Import: the #1546 tessellation cap (25 M evaluations) falsely refuses healthy STEP faces; a tripped finer pass refuses the whole model
