body:
Regression from PR #1546 (#1536, merged 5aab848f): the per-face tessellation evaluation cap `FACE_EVAL_CAP` (25 M, `crates/app/src/geometry/import/step_guard.rs:45`) falsely refuses healthy STEP models.

**Evidence** (M5's review of #1546, pullrequestreview-5898774979, posted after the merge):
- Corpus: 75 STEP files (testdata plus a user's project library). Measured peak evaluations on one face in one pass: 32050.STEP 23.1 M (**92 % of the cap**), socket-head screws 16-19 M, 10208 / 22588B 7.3 M. A healthy face can need far more than the "a few million" the code comment and `docs/decisions/1536-step-tess-guard.md` claim.
- **A false refusal:** `10208.STEP` at the user-settable facet budget of 60 M (`step_budget::CEILING`). On main before #1546 it imports (14,866,333 facets at chord 5e-3, 173 s). After #1546 it is refused as "did not converge" on face #1073, which actually converged at 28.07 M evaluations.
- **Why the whole model fails:** the trip returns `Err(Step)` through `step_refine::refine`, which refuses the whole model. Before, a failed finer pass kept the coarser mesh.

**Expected:**
- A face that converges is never refused at any allowed budget. Give the cap real headroom (e.g. about 10x; about 12-15 s on a broken face in release), or scale it with the facet budget.
- When a finer refinement pass trips the cap, keep the coarser pass's mesh (with a note) instead of refusing the whole model, as before #1546.
- The truly non-converging face (the #1536 case) is still refused by name in bounded time.

**Done means:** 10208.STEP imports at the 60 M budget as before; a pin shows that a face converging past the old cap is not refused; the #1536 synthetic and sc_logo cases still refuse by name within bounded time; and the comment and decision file carry the measured corpus numbers.

Related: #1536, PR #1546, #1545, #1548.

title: Setups page: "Pick for WCS" takes no viewport pick - clicks still select the whole model

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Reported by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat, on a v0.19.0 build): "this section under Setup<n> is to set WCS - but it cannot really select any edges, points or gizmo axises.. so not sure what its supposed todo?" Priority P1 is the maintainer's ("Make P1 issue for it").

What happens: on the Setups page, the row "Set WCS from features - each pick sets a role" is armed with "Pick for WCS". The status line says to pick faces, edges, corners or walls, but a click in the viewport selects the whole model as usual. Nothing is highlighted on hover, no "Picked: ..." line appears, and Apply never becomes available.

What should happen (issue 701, the row's own hover text): while the row collects, a click on a face, an edge, a corner or a curved wall is taken as the pick for the role in the box (Origin, X, Y, Z), and the hover highlights what the click would take.

Cause, from the code:
- `crates/ui/src/interact.rs` (about lines 104-108) sends a viewport click to `feature_click::click` only when `state.geo_pick` is Face, Edge or Vertex. In `GeoPick::Model`, the default (`state.rs`), the click goes to `pick_model`. The hover has the same gate (about line 185).
- `crates/ui/src/wcs_pick.rs` `arm` leaves `geo_pick` as it is, on purpose ("the toolbar's pick mode is the user's own"). Every other pick draft switches it when armed: `plane_pick` (Face), `points_pick` (Vertex), `axis_pick` (`mode_of(by)`), `locate_pick` (Face), the boundary pick (Model to Edge).
- The only control that changes the mode is "Click selects:" on an operation's Geometry page (`egui_app/geo_page.rs`), which is not shown on the Setups page. So with no operation open the mode is Model and the role draft can never receive a pick. `feature_click::ask` and `click` already handle the armed row correctly (faces, edges and points together); they are just never reached.
- Why the tests did not catch it: `egui_app/wcs_pick_tests.rs` sets `geo_pick = GeoPick::Vertex` by hand or calls `wcs_pick::take` directly. No test arms the row from the default mode and clicks through `interact`.

Not a defect: the gizmo axes are not a pick target of this row by design. If picking a gizmo axis as a role is wanted, that is a separate enhancement.

Suggested fix: while `wcs_pick::collecting(state)`, route viewport clicks and hover to `feature_click` whatever `geo_pick` is (as `wcs_ui.pick_circle` already does for the hover), or have `arm` leave Model mode and restore the previous mode on disarm, pause and Apply. Check the same gate for any other draft that relies on the mode it sets being left alone.

Done means: from a fresh project (pick mode Model, no operation open), arming "Pick for WCS" and clicking a face, an edge and a corner in the viewport records each as "Picked: ..." with its role, the hover highlights the feature under the cursor, and Apply places the WCS; pinned by a ui test that arms the row from the default mode and drives the click through `interact` (not `wcs_pick::take`); disarming gives the previous click behaviour back.

title: Circular writes each ring as 512 chords with no arcs: one 6 mm hole is 74,131 moves

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5**: **still reproduces, identical move counts**.

## What happens

One Ø6 mm through hole (10 mm deep plate, 11 mm cut) with a Circular op and a 4 mm end mill came out as **74,131 moves** (53 rapids, 74,078 feeds, median feed length **0.0061 mm**, no arcs). Posted, that is about 74,000 G1 blocks for one small hole: a huge file, and at 500 mm/min each block lasts under 1 ms, far past what most controls can process, so the machine starves and stutters. The user dropped Circular and used the Bore op (arcs) instead.

Every parameter set tried is in the tens of thousands:

| Circular params (others as below) | moves | median segment |
|---|---|---|
| as below (helix entry R1, stepover 0.5) | 74,131 | 0.0061 mm |
| `entry: plunge` | 13,416 | 0.0123 mm |
| `helix_radius: 0.5` | 13,446 | 0.0123 mm (+ warnings `feed moves 2 and 6737 cross in XY at shared depth`) |
| `stepover: 1.0` or `2.0` | 26,937 | 0.0123 mm |
| `radius: 4.0` | 26,858 | 0.0184 mm |
| `radius: 6.0` | 53,690 | 0.0307 mm |
| `stepdown: 2.0` | 67,989 | 0.0061 mm |

**Cause (read, not fixed).** `ring_loop` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/circular.rs` writes every ring as a closed polygon of **512 chords** whatever its radius, and the op emits no arcs. A ring at R1 (6 mm hole, 4 mm tool) is 512 chords of 0.012 mm each, at every level. The helix entry ("stands down to a ramp along the first cut") then ramps along that polygon, splitting it further, which is where the 74k comes from. The Bore op on the same hole emits three arcs per ring.

## Minimal repro (MCP)

```
import_model   {"path": "End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step", "name": "part"}
move_model     {"name": "part", "position": [0, 37.9, 4.826]}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 110, "dy": 185, "dz": 15.33}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0400-2FL", "name": "EM4"}
add_operation  {"kind": "Circular", "tool": "EM4", "name": "c", "source": "part",
                "params": {"center": [-35.0, 2.9], "radius": 3.0, "stepover": 0.5,
                           "top_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -0.508},
                           "bottom_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -11.524},
                           "stepdown": 1.0, "feed": 500, "plunge_feed": 250, "climb": true,
```

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5**: **still reproduces, identical hole list and path**.

The user's part (`End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step`, FreeCAD): a plate 101.6 x 177.4 x 10 mm with one Ø74.305 mm through bore and four Ø6 mm through holes.

## What happens

1. `detect_holes` on a Bore op (tool: catalog `EM-0400-2FL`, a 4 mm end mill) lists **5 holes**: the four Ø6 holes **and the Ø74.3 bore** (`"radius": 37.152667, "through": true`). There is no size limit relative to the tool or the op, and no note.
2. Generated as is, the Bore op machines the Ø74.3 bore like a small hole. At each 2 mm level it **plunges the 4 mm end mill at the bore centre**, feeds a full-width straight slot 35.15 mm out to the wall, retracts to clearance, re-plunges at the wall and runs one ring at R35.15. The result is a groove round the wall plus one slot, leaving a **Ø66 mm core disc** in the middle, which breaks free at the last level when nothing under the part holds it. `generate` says `ok`, `verify` says `ok: true` with no findings or warnings, and the program posts.

From the path (main, part bottom at z 4.826; moves 155-163, one level):

```
rapid  (0, 37.9, 40.33) -> (0, 37.9, 16.826)
plunge (0, 37.9, 16.826) -> (0, 37.9, 14.826)        <- centre of the Ø74 bore, into solid
feed   (0, 37.9, 14.826) -> (35.153, 37.9, 14.826)   <- full-width slot to the wall
rapid  up to 40.33, back down to 16.826 at (35.153, 37.9)
plunge -> 14.826 ; three arcs: one ring at R35.153
```

In the user's project the bore was removed from the list by hand (and roughed with a 2D Adaptive instead).

## Minimal repro (MCP)

```
import_model   {"path": "End Caps-End capSupport Plate.step", "name": "part"}
move_model     {"name": "part", "position": [0, 37.9, 4.826]}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 110, "dy": 185, "dz": 15.33}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0400-2FL", "name": "EM4"}
add_operation  {"kind": "Bore", "tool": "EM4", "name": "Bore", "source": "part", "params": {"stepdown": 2.0}}
detect_holes   {"name": "Bore"}   -> "holes": 5 (one of radius 37.152667)
generate {} ; verify {}           -> ok, no findings
```

Any plate with one hole much larger than the tool (e.g. a Ø40 bore with a 6 mm tool) shows the same.

## Expected

- Hole detection for a Drill, Bore or Thread op leaves out holes the op's tool cannot make as a hole, and says so: for a Bore op, a hole wider than the size a single helical or circular pass clears without leaving a core (about two tool diameters); for Drill, a hole that is not the drill's size. A note names what was skipped ("Ø74.3 bore skipped: wider than 2 x the 4 mm tool - use a pocket or adaptive"), or the threshold is a visible setting.
- A Bore op given such a hole by hand (edited list) either clears the core (spirals out from the centre helix) or refuses by name. It never plunges into solid at the centre and leaves a free core with an `ok` verdict.

## Done means

- `detect_holes` on the user's plate (or a plate with a Ø40 bore and a 6 mm tool) lists only the holes the op can make, with a note naming each skipped bore and why; pinned by a test.
- A Bore op holding a hole whose ring would leave a core either clears it or refuses at generate with the hole named; pinned by a test.

The through-hole floor rule is #1557.

title: 2D Contour and the 2D Pocket wall pass run conventional when climb is true (outside CCW, inside CW with M3)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP, Tormach PathPilot post. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5**: **still reproduces, identical directions**.

## What happens

With `climb: true` (the default, shown in the GUI as "Climb milling"), **2D Contour runs conventional**: with the spindle on M3 the outside profile runs **CCW** around the part and an inside (bore) profile runs **CW**. With `climb: false` it runs the other way, which is the real climb. Every 2D contour posted with the default flag is conventional-milled, silently. In the user's project the three contours had to be set to `climb: false` to get climb.

The **2D Pocket**'s wall pass shares the inversion. Other ops are right:

| Op (`climb: true`, M3) | Measured travel at the floor | Correct for climb? |
|---|---|---|
| 2D Contour, outside | CCW (G3 corners) | **no** (conventional) |
| 2D Contour, inside (bore) | CW | **no** (conventional) |
| 2D Pocket, bore wall pass | CW | **no** (conventional) |
| 2D Adaptive, in the bore | CCW (G3) | yes |
| Bore | CCW (G3) | yes |
| Circular | CCW | yes |

Posted output (main, outside contour, `climb: true`; the part spans X ±50, Y ±30):

```
S9500 M3
...
G01 X50.346 Y-32.98 Z-2 F1200
G03 X53 Y-30 Z-2 I-0.346 J2.98 F1200
G01 X53 Y30 Z-2 F1200
G03 X50 Y33 Z-2 I-3 J0 F1200
G01 X-50 Y33 Z-2 F1200
```

That is the tool going up the +X side and across the top to -X: CCW around the part.

**The convention.** With M3 (clockwise spindle seen from above), climb milling keeps the material on the **right** of the tool's travel (the G41 side): an outside profile runs **clockwise** around the part, an inside profile (a hole or pocket wall) runs **counter-clockwise**. Conventional is the reverse. With M4 both reverse.

**Cause (read, not fixed).** `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs` (around line 207) says "Canonical orientation is material-on-the-left travel; conventional climbing reverses it", and keeps that order when `p.climb != inside`. Material on the left of the travel with M3 is conventional, so the rule is inverted. The unit test `contour_inside_shrinks_and_flips_travel` in `machining2d/tests.rs` pins the same reading ("climb under Inside travels the loop reversed, so material stays on the left"). The GUI label maps 1:1 to the parameter, so the parameter, not the label, is what is wrong. The pocket's wall pass needs the same check (`pocket.rs` / `pocket_hsm.rs` `plan_passes`); also worth checking 2D Chamfer, Slot, Trace and the contour lead/arc side (`arc_leads.rs` `air_side`), which follow the same flag.

## Minimal repro (MCP)

`plate_bore.stl`: a 100 x 60 x 10 mm plate, centred in XY, z 0..10, with a centred Ø40 through bore.

```
import_model   {"path": "plate_bore.stl", "name": "plate"}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 120, "dy": 80, "dz": 12}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "EM6"}
add_operation  {"kind": "2D Contour", "tool": "EM6", "name": "outside", "source": "plate",
                "params": {"top_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -2},
                           "bottom_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -11},
                           "stepdown": 20, "climb": true, "entry": "plunge"}}
set_operation_geometry {"operation": "outside", "picks": [the 4 top outer edges' chains]}
edit_operation {"name": "outside", "params": {"side": "outside"}}
(same again, "inside", picking the bore's top chain, side "inside")
generate {} ; post {"output": "out.nc"}
```

Result: outside CCW, inside CW (signed area of the floor-level feed moves +7276 / -915 mm²). With `climb: false`: outside CW, inside CCW.

## Expected

`climb: true` with M3: outside profiles CW, inside profiles CCW, on every 2D op that takes the flag (and both reversed under M4), matching Adaptive, Bore and Circular today.

## Done means

- 2D Contour (outside, inside, open chains) and the 2D Pocket wall pass run climb as defined above when `climb: true`, conventional when false; pinned by a direction test per op that checks the signed travel at a level against the spindle direction.
- Every other op with a `climb` flag (Chamfer, Slot, Trace, Face rows, leads) checked against the same rule and pinned.
- The test that pins "material on the left" is corrected, not deleted; affected CL/NC goldens are regenerated in one commit.
- The release notes say that contour and pocket direction changed: a project that set `climb: false` as a workaround will now post conventional.

title: 2D Adaptive with the stock as source clears the part's own section (generate says ok, only verify stops it); a band narrower than the tool is skipped silently

body:
Found while programming a simple 2.5D end-cap plate (user's project) with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP. Re-checked on upstream main **d00243a5** (`camcraft-cli` built from it): **still reproduces, identical output**.

The user's part: a FreeCAD plate 101.6 x 177.4 x 10 mm with a Ø74.3 mm through bore and 4 x Ø6 mm through holes, in a box stock 0.125 in larger per side. The aim was to rough the outside of the part with a 2D Adaptive whose source is the stock (as on an earlier project).

## What happens

A 2D Adaptive with `source: "stock"` and no geometry picks clears the **whole stock footprint**, the part included, to full depth. `generate` reports the op `ok` with no warning and no note. Only `verify` catches it, and blocks the post:

- the user's plate: `gouge: program cuts below the model in 85918 cell(s), worst 11.02 mm`. Same with an exclude boundary on the bore, and with the part unrotated.
- the minimal repro below (a plain 100 x 60 x 10 box, no bore at all): `gouge: program cuts below the model in 42560 cell(s), worst 9.00 mm at (-49.69, -29.69, z 1.00)`. With a centred Ø40 bore in it: 33634 cells, worst 9.00 mm. 1066 of the 1740 feed points sit inside the part outline below its top.

Nothing unsafe is posted (verify holds the post). But generate hands back a path that cuts through the part and calls it `ok`.

**Second finding, same goal (rough a plate's outside in a slightly larger stock).** With `source: "plate"` (the model) the adaptive does protect the part. But when the stock margin is narrower than the tool (3.175 mm per side with a 6 mm tool, the user's 0.125 in), the outside band is **dropped silently**: the op comes back `ok` with no note and no warnings, and every one of its 51,188 feed points is inside the bore; the outside is not cut at all. The user's attempt to limit the adaptive to that band with picks was refused instead: `pocket is narrower than the tool`. An outside band is open to air on its outer side, so a tool wider than the band can still cut it (one pass along the part, hanging over the stock edge).

## Minimal repro (MCP)

`plate.stl`: a closed 100 x 60 x 10 mm box, centred in XY, z 0..10 (12 facets).

```
import_model   {"path": "plate.stl", "name": "plate"}
add_setup      {"name": "Setup 1"}
set_stock      {"box": {"dx": 120, "dy": 80, "dz": 12}}
set_wcs        {"stock_point": {"x": "center", "y": "center", "z": "max"}}
add_tool       {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "EM6"}
add_operation  {"kind": "2D Adaptive", "tool": "EM6", "name": "outside rough", "source": "stock",
                "params": {"top_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": 0},
                           "bottom_z": {"reference": "top_of_stock", "offset": -11}, "stepdown": 4}}
generate {}   -> status "ok", 882 moves, 0 warnings
verify {}     -> ok: false, "gouge: program cuts below the model in 42560 cell(s), worst 9.00 mm ..."
```

Same calls with `"source": "plate"`: 318 moves, all outside the part, verify clean (the expected behaviour). With `"source": "plate"`, a Ø40 bore in the plate and the stock at 106.35 x 66.35 (3.175 mm margin): `ok`, no note, the outside not cut.

## Expected

- A stock-sourced 2D Adaptive in a setup that holds a part never machines the part's own section: it roughs the stock minus the part (the outside band, and nothing inside the part outline unless picked), or it refuses at generate by name ("the stock source covers the part - pick the area or use the model as the source"). Compare #12 (the same law for a whole-model Pocket source) and #3.
- An outside band narrower than the tool is still roughed (the tool may hang over the open stock edge), or the op says plainly that the band was skipped and why. Never a silent `ok` that left the outside uncut.

## Done means

- The minimal repro above (stock source, plain box) generates a path with no cut inside the part outline below its top, or is refused at generate with a message naming the cause; pinned by a test.
- A model-sourced adaptive with a stock margin narrower than the tool either cuts the band or carries a note/warning naming the skipped band; pinned by a test.
- `verify` stays the backstop; no existing gouge pin is loosened.

Related: #12, #3, #1446.

title: Sim/carry: an outside contour leaves full-height slivers at the stock's outer corners in the carried body (probe needed)

body:
Found while building pins for PR #1549 (#1530). Not yet probed; please confirm before fixing.

**Observation:** a 50 x 50 x 10 mm part in **60 x 60** stock, with a Setup 1 outside 2D Contour using a 15.24 mm (0.6 in) end mill down to Z 4. The carried stock body for Setup 2 (`rest::entered_body` dexel columns) kept roughly **1.5 mm triangles at the stock's four outer corners at full stock height**. That is why #1549's pins use 56 x 56 stock instead.

**Why it looks wrong** (an analysis from the other session): the contour's tool reaches about 15 mm from the part's corner, while the stock corner is only 7.07 mm from the part corner (5 mm per side), so the corners should be cut through. A full-height sliver there is a sim or carry gap, not true rest material. Either the contour's corner motion (an arc vs an extended corner) or the dexel carry at the stock's outer boundary columns.

**Probe first:**
1. Reproduce with 60 x 60 stock and dump the posted path around one corner.
2. Compute the swept tool disc at the stock corner analytically.
3. Compare with the carried body's columns there, and with the in-setup stock sim (not carried).

If the path covers the corner but the carried body keeps it, it's a carry or sim bug: in Setup 2 it can make a fixture or vise falsely collide, or report false rest. If the path really leaves it, it's a contour corner-motion issue.

**Done means:** the probe result is posted here. If a bug, a pin with the 60 x 60 case shows no full-height corner material after the contour, sim-verified, plus the fix.

Related: #1530, PR #1549 (pins work around it with 56 x 56 stock).

body:
Found while fixing #1543.

What happens: a Circular whose source is a pick (a round pocket's floor face, or a bore's rim) takes `DepthLaw::None` (`depth_law_of`, `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`), so its path is never judged against the part it was picked off. Reading: the `circular_pick.rs` fixture (a 40 x 40 x 8 block with a radius-15 round pocket, floor at Z 3), the floor face picked, Bottom typed Z 1: the rings cut to Z 1, 2 mm into the part under the floor, and the operation carries **0 warnings** (status ok, no `Warning::Gouge`, MCP `verify` lists no operation finding). Only the program-level post gate's stock sim catches it: `post blocked - gouge: program cuts below the model in 1202 cell(s), worst 2.00 mm at (-6.31, -8.31, z 1.00)`.

So the post is held (not a P1), but the operation reads clean, names no moves, and nothing holds it where the program sim is not run (a single op verify, the preview).

Expected: a picked Circular is judged against the part like the picked pocket family and the picked Slot (#1504): `DepthLaw::Section` (or the shared `authored_law` of #1543 widened to picks), so the op itself carries the blocking Gouge on the moves under the floor; a legal picked circle (the existing `circular_pick.rs` cases) stays clean.

Watch for: a typed-true circle against a coarse tessellated wall at stock-to-leave 0 is convicted by the chord sagitta under `Section` (see `docs/decisions/1543-circular-entity-law.md`); a pick hands the fitted circle, so the same read applies.

Done means: a picked-floor Circular cut below its floor carries a blocking `Warning::Gouge` on the operation; the `circular_pick.rs` cases stay clean; MCP verify names the operation's gouge.

Refs #1543

title: Import: tessellate B-spline corner blends (three-fillet corners) that truck cannot divide, instead of refusing them

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

body:
Follow-up to #1536 and PR #1546. With #1546, a STEP whose NURBS face the tessellator cannot converge on is **refused by name in about 3 s** instead of hanging. That is safe, but the model still cannot be used.

**The case:** a 30 mm cube with every edge filleted about 2-3 mm, exported from SolidCraft 0.41.0 as STEP (sha256 08c498b5…). PR #1546's repro on d569372f refuses it: "face #836 (NURBS surface, face 9 of 62 in shell #3148) could not be tessellated ... did not converge within 25000000 evaluations ... re-export the model, or import an STL". The faces that fail are the B-spline corner blends where three fillets meet, which is a very common shape: any part with all edges rounded has them. The same model imports as an STL from SolidCraft without trouble (51,540 triangles at about 0.003 mm chord).

**Expected:** CamCraft tessellates these blends (they are well-formed in the file: closed solid, volume 19549.71 mm³ matches SolidCraft), within the facet and time budgets, so ordinary rounded parts import from STEP.

**Notes:** #1546 found that truck's `sub_parameter_division` does not converge on non-continuous B-spline/NURBS faces. Options: our own adaptive or uniform parametric tessellator for B-spline faces (bounded by chord error and an evaluation cap); knot-span splitting at the discontinuities before division; or a fallback grid at the chord tolerance when division fails, judged against the face's bounds. Record the choice and its literature in a decision file.

**Done means:** the filleted-cube STEP imports, and its mesh volume is within the chord tolerance of the STEP's stated volume. A pin uses a minimal STEP with one three-fillet corner blend. Faces that still cannot be meshed keep #1546's by-name refusal.

Found on a user's real part (the h5/sc_logo HAT project). Related: #1536, #1545 (edge and swept divisions unmetered).

body:
Found while fixing #1529 (the Top/Bottom of Model heights, which now read only the parts through `setup_align::part_aabb_in`).

What happens (code reading, upstream/main 41cd9c2): the GUI's stock fit (`crates/ui/src/state.rs` ~3059, 3071, 3089: box fit, cylinder radius via `solid_radius_about_in`, and the second fit path) and the stock info strip (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/stock_info.rs:13`) read `setup_align::solid_aabb_in`, which walks every `model::model_entities` entry - fixtures included. With a vise, soft jaw, plate or tagged fixture placed, "fit stock to models" sizes the stock around the workholding, not the part.

Expected: fitting the stock to the models measures the parts only (the same set #1529's `part_aabb_in` uses; the cylinder fit needs a part-only radius twin of `solid_radius_about_in`). Collision checks keep seeing the fixtures.

Not exercised: no test drives this yet; this is from reading the callers. The MCP `set_stock` fit path should be checked for the same set.

Done means: with a vise placed, the GUI box and cylinder fits and the stock info read the part's bounds; a pinning test per fit kind with and without a vise gives the same stock.

Related: #1529, #1094.

title: Slot with a whole-model (entity) source cuts through the finished part with no gouge warning

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while fixing the review of PR #1522 (#1504).

What happens: a plain Slot whose source is a whole model (`SrcRef::Entity("part")`) or the stock takes no part law: `depth_law_of` (`crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs`, the `_ => DepthLaw::None` arm) gives a Slot `DepthLaw::Section` only when its source is a Selection. So a typed slot through the part's pocket wall generates and posts with no gouge warning, even when the job knows the source model is the finished part (`part_solid` is true). It is pinned as today's behaviour by `with_nothing_picked_the_typed_endpoints_rule_as_before` in `crates/app/tests/slot_picks.rs`: Entity("part") source, slot (-20,0)-(20,0) width 12 cut through the 30 x 16 pocket's walls at x 15, no `Warning::Gouge`.

Why P1: #1504's own third bullet (the maintainer's report) expects "With nothing selected, the typed endpoints still work, and the model gouge check still decides." Today nothing decides, so a gouge into the finished part passes to the post. The code comment's contract ("the source is the material to remove, not a part to keep") holds for a Stock source, but not when the named model is the finished part.

Expected: with an entity source that is the finished part, the Slot is judged against it (`DepthLaw::Section`, as for a picked Slot) and a slot through a wall is convicted as a blocking Gouge. A Stock source keeps today's behaviour. The same question applies to Circular (same arm); decide it with this issue or file it separately.

Done means: a test with an Entity("part") Slot cut through the pocket wall gets a blocking `Warning::Gouge` and the post is held; a Stock source still cuts the typed slot unjudged; `with_nothing_picked_the_typed_endpoints_rule_as_before` is updated to the new law.

Refs #1504

title: Import: a STEP of a 30 mm filleted cube never finishes

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1

labels.name: area:3d

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (`camcraft-cli 0.19.0`, macOS arm64).

## What happens

Importing `sc_logo.step` **never finishes**. The STEP was exported by SolidCraft 0.41.0, and its bounding box and volume match the design. Under CamCraft v0.19.0 the import:

- ran for **over 19 CPU-minutes** in the user's session without finishing;
- ran the same way with `facet_budget: 200000`;
- **re-run for this issue:** `cam.import("sc_logo.step", "sc_logo")` through `camcraft-cli script`, killed after **10 min 13 s wall (10 min 10 s CPU, 322 MB resident)** with no output and no error (see below).

Nothing in the import is bounded in time. The facet budget does not stop it, because no facet is ever produced. A hang on user input breaks the Prime Directive: the import must finish or refuse by name.

## The model

A **30 mm cube made of two L-shaped halves**:
- the top half is missing the +X+Y quadrant and the bottom half the -X-Y quadrant, which makes two 15 mm-deep quadrant steps;
- **every edge is filleted R3.125 mm**, convex and concave.

STEP content:
- 1 closed shell, 62 faces, 126 edges, 66 vertices;
- the faces are 12 planes, 30 cylinders, 14 spheres and **20 `B_SPLINE_SURFACE_WITH_KNOTS`**, the blends where three fillets meet;
- 106 `B_SPLINE_CURVE_WITH_KNOTS` edges, AP242, 198 KB.

SolidCraft reports the volume as 19549.7 mm3 and the bbox as +/-15 mm.

## Where it spins

`sample` of the process after 4 min (one core busy, all other rayon workers idle). The busy thread is:

```
camcraft_app::script::api::v_import
 camcraft_app::commands::import_model::ImportModel::within
  camcraft_app::geometry::import::load_model_graded_within
   camcraft_app::geometry::import::step::parse_with_chord_budget
    camcraft_app::geometry::import::step_refine::refine<..., step::shell_facets>
     camcraft_app::geometry::import::step::shell_facets
      truck_meshalgo::tessellation::triangulation::cshell_tessellation<..., by_search_nearest_parameter>
       (rayon par_iter over CompressedFace)
        truck_geotrait::algo::surface::sub_parameter_division<NurbsSurface<Vector4>>
         truck_geometry::nurbs::knot_vec::KnotVec::try_bspline_basis_functions   <- top of stack, most samples
```

So one face's tessellation, very likely one of the 20 NURBS corner blends, never converges in truck's `sub_parameter_division`. The `within` / chord-budget wrapper cannot interrupt it, because the loop is inside truck.

A second sample at 7.7 min shows the same frames. The resident memory grew from 175 MB (at 4 min) to 322 MB (at 7.7 min), so the subdivision keeps refining rather than spinning in place.

## Reproduction

1. Rebuild the STEP: replay the SolidCraft script below with SolidCraft 0.41.0 (`solidcraft-cli eval sc_logo.script.json`), then export STEP (`file.export {"path": "sc_logo.step"}`, or `export {path}` over SolidCraft's MCP).
2. Import it headlessly:

```js
// imp.js
cam.import("sc_logo.step", "sc_logo");
```
```
timeout 600 camcraft-cli script imp.js      # never returns
```

The MCP `import_model {path: "sc_logo.step"}` hangs the same way; so does `import_model` with `facet_budget: 200000`.

## Expected

The import finishes within a bounded time, or refuses **by name**. For example: `face 37 (B-spline surface) could not be tessellated within N s / M subdivisions - re-export the model, or import an STL`. No input file can hang the importer.

- A per-face (and per-import) iteration or time bound around the tessellation call, ending in a named refusal.
- Better, the NURBS blends tessellate. They are ordinary fillet corner patches.

**Done means:** `sc_logo.step` (built from the script above) imports in seconds with a closed mesh whose volume matches 19549.7 mm3 within the chord tolerance, or is refused by name in under a minute. A pinning test imports it (or a minimal STEP with one of its blend faces) under a hard time limit, and a guard test feeds a pathological NURBS face and asserts a named refusal, not a hang.

Related: #27 (Solidcore replaces the B-rep engine), #916 (STEP import through solidcore-step).

body:
What happens: the GUI sets the post options (Skip pauses and homes, Output one-file-per-operation, Threading, End units) through the undoable `SetPostOptions` (document) and `SetSetupPostOptions` (a setup's own, #389), but the MCP server has no tool for either - nothing under `crates/app/src/mcp/` names `PostOptions`. An agent cannot read or change what a program posts with.

Expected: a `set_post_options` tool (and a read in its result or a `get_post_options`) taking the option fields and an optional `setup`: with `setup`, that setup's own options (`SetSetupPostOptions`); without, the document's (`SetPostOptions`) - stated explicitly, as `load_machine` does, so an agent always names its target (no implicit routing, so no #1526-style bleed). Plus a way to make a setup follow the document again (`setup` + `follow: true`), and the camcraft-mcp skill row.

Evidence: found while fixing #1526 (GUI post options bled from Setup2 into Setup1). The MCP path has no bleed only because it has no tool. #1390 plans an MCP `set_post_options` for its Explain switch; this issue is the base tool for the existing options, which #1390 can extend.

Done means: an MCP test sets an option on Setup2 with `setup`, Setup1's resolved options are unchanged, undo restores; a call without `setup` sets the document's; the camcraft-mcp skill lists the tool.

Related: #1526, #1390, #389.

Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP, Tormach PathPilot post.

## What happens

A document with two setups (Setup 1 at G54, Setup 2 at G55, with the part flipped between them) posts as **one program**. Setup 2's first operation follows Setup 1's last move with **no program stop** (`M0`/`M1`) and no message to the operator. From the posted file:

```
G1 X1.3127 Y-1.0908 Z-0.2962 F30
G0 X1.3127 Y-1.0908 Z0.9843
M9
M5
(SETUP: Setup 2)
(OPERATION: S2 Face hat off rough - FACE - G55)
G17 G90 G55 G40 G49 G80
...
T31 M6
G43 H31
S9500 M3
M8
```

On cycle start, the machine finishes Setup 1 and **starts cutting Setup 2's path at once**, before anyone has flipped or re-clamped the part. Setup 2's program is then running on a part still clamped for Setup 1. It cuts air at best; at worst it cuts the wrong side of the part, the vise or the parallels at full feed.

To get one program per setup, the user had to delete the other setup's ops from a scratch copy and post again, or cut the file apart by hand.

A per-operation "after" action already exists (`AfterOperation`: optional stop / program stop / go home, #110), and a program-stop entry can be put after an op in the GUI. **Nothing puts one at a setup boundary by default**, and I found no MCP tool that adds a stop entry.

## Expected

The user chooses, per document (and in the post dialog / MCP `post`), between:

1. **one file per setup** (for example `name_setup1.nc`, `name_setup2.nc`, each with its own header, tool list, work offset and `M30`); or
2. **one file with a stop between setups**: an `M0` (or `M1` if the user prefers) after the last op of each setup, with a comment naming the next setup and what to do (`(SETUP 2: FLIP PART, CLAMP ..., G55)`).

**Safety:** the default for a multi-setup document posted as one file should be the `M0` stop, not "run straight on". A program that moves from one setup to the next with no pause is a crash waiting for an operator who expects it to stop. The current default may deserve a higher priority than this issue carries.

**Done means:** posting a two-setup document either writes one file per setup, or writes one file with an `M0` and a setup-change comment between the setups, as chosen. With no choice made, the default never runs from one setup into the next without a stop. The MCP `post` tool takes the choice. A pinning post test covers both modes on at least the Fanuc and Tormach dialects.

Related: #110 (per-operation after-action), #388 (one file per post when setups use different machines), #258 (post dialog options).

title: Second setups: fixtures in a flipped (aligned) setup are judged by bounding box

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P2
labels.description: Main is broken or a regression with no workaround; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP.

## What happens

In a second setup that takes "what Setup 1 leaves behind" as its stock (part flipped, part alignment), the carried-workholding gate judges each fixture by its **world bounding box**, not its shape. Any fixture whose box encloses the carried part is refused, even when the steel only touches the part's sides.

Cause (v0.19.0): `crates/app/src/fixture_carried.rs::carried_fixture_problems` reads `model::entity_world_aabb(world, &fe)` and passes that box to `penetration()`. Every carried column whose centre lies inside the box's XY footprint and whose material overlaps its Z span counts as a hit.

Refusals seen:

1. **The built-in vise** (`add_builtin_vise`, 5 in, jaws closed on a 50 mm part): its box spans the opening between the jaws, so the part it clamps "stands inside" it.
   `setup 'Setup 2': fixture 'Vise 5 in (2)' stands inside the stock carried from setup 'Setup 1' (4.48 mm deep) - the part that setup leaves cannot be held as modelled; move the fixture or re-check the hold`
2. **A pair of 5.2 x 2 x 1 in aluminum soft jaws with a nest pocket**, imported as one STEP fixture, with the part seated in the nest:
   `fixture 'Soft jaws (nest)' stands inside the stock carried from setup 'Setup 1' (11.43 mm deep) - the part that setup leaves cannot be held as modelled`
   The nest is inside the jaws' box, so the part is "inside the fixture" by definition.
3. The same jaws modelled as 9 plain blocks cut around the nest: the jaw "island" blocks are still refused at **9.93 and 11.28 mm** deep. Those island blocks lie inside the nest's L-shaped notch, below the part's notch floor (3.57 mm clearance as designed). Part of this may be that the Setup 1 3D ops were held, so the carried body there is not fully cut. The box-based judging is the same either way.

The workaround in the user's h5 project: model the vise jaws as two separate blocks instead of the built-in vise.

## Reproduction (headless, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

- The h5 plate: a 50 x 50 x 6 mm plate with 5 mm grooves.
- Setup 1 (top side) machines it from 55 x 55 x 11.3 mm stock in a vise.
- Setup 2 flips it about X (part alignment), uses "what Setup 1 leaves behind", and holds it in two block jaws plus parallels. That verifies and posts clean.
- Then, in Setup 2, place the built-in vise where the block jaws are:

```
open_project {path: h5.camproj}
add_builtin_vise {size: "5 in", setup: "Setup 2", position: [0, 25, -28.798], opening: 50}
verify
post {output: o.nc}
```

-> `verify.gate.problems` and the post refusal: `setup 'Setup 2': fixture 'Vise 5 in (2)' stands inside the stock carried from setup 'Setup 1' (4.48 mm deep) ...`

The vise's jaw faces are at Y +/-25, exactly the part's 50 mm sides. The steel only touches the part; the box reaches across it.

## Expected

The carried-stock fixture check judges the fixture's **real solid**: its mesh, or each body of a multi-body fixture, such as each jaw of a vise or each jaw of a soft-jaw pair. A part seated in a nest pocket, or clamped between jaws, passes. Steel truly inside the carried material is still refused by name.

**Done means:** a built-in vise clamping a carried part on its sides, and an imported soft-jaw fixture with a nest the carried part sits in, both pass the carried-workholding gate. A fixture that really overlaps the carried material (a jaw block moved into the part) is still refused with its depth. Pinning tests cover all three.

Not checked here: whether the in-setup fixture collision check (toolpath vs fixture) has the same box-only limit. It passed for the nest program in a single setup.

Related: #321 (the carried-workholding clause), #637 (carried stock on the field engine), #1511 (soft-jaw presets with a nest).

title: Heights: 'Top/Bottom of Model' include the fixtures, so cuts follow the vise

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
Found while programming a small two-sided part with HAT-style stock and soft jaws (user's project), with the CamCraft **v0.19.0** release CLI (macOS arm64), driven headlessly over MCP.

## What happens

`Top of Model` and `Bottom of Model` resolve to the bounds of **every model in the document, fixtures included**. With a vise placed, a cut referenced to `Bottom of Model` runs down to the **bottom of the vise body**, and `Top of Model` can resolve to the **jaw tops**.

Every 2D/3D milling kind defaults to these references: 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, Slot, Trace, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset, Engrave, Circular, 3D Pocket, 3D Finish, Deburr and Trochoidal slot (`bottom_z = bottom_of_model`, `top_z = top_of_model`), plus 2D Chamfer and Thread (`top_z`). So a default operation in a document with a vise is wrong at generate.

Cause (v0.19.0): `operation/heights.rs` resolves both references through `setup_align::solid_aabb_in` -> `model::solid_world_aabb`, which walks `model::model_entities`. `model::is_model` leaves out stock, WCS, tools, operations, setups and program entries, but **not fixtures**. The fixture's setup is not considered either.

## Reproduction (headless, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

A plain 50 x 50 x 6 mm block (STL), moved to Z 4..10. Box stock 55 x 55 x 11 (Z 0..11). WCS at the stock top centre. Tool `EM-0600-4FL`. One `2D Contour` with its defaults (top = Top of Model, bottom = Bottom of Model).

```
import_model {path: block.stl, name: block}
move_model   {name: block, position: [-25, -25, 4]}
set_stock    {box: {dx: 55, dy: 55, dz: 11}}
set_wcs      {stock_point: {x: center, y: center, z: max}}
add_builtin_vise {size: "5 in", position: [0, 27.5, -36.1], opening: 55}   # jaw tops at Z 2, below the part
add_tool     {catalog: EM-0600-4FL}
add_operation {kind: "2D Contour", tool: EM-0600-4FL, name: Op, source: block}
generate; verify; post {output: out.nc, post: Fanuc}
```

| | Bottom of Model resolves to | Top of Model resolves to | Generate | Verify / post |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No vise | Z 4 (part bottom), posted Z-7.0 | Z 10 | ok | ok, posts levels Z-1 / -6 / -7 |
| Vise below the part (jaw tops Z 2) | **Z -99.6, the vise base** (WCS Z -110.6) | Z 10 | **ok, no warning** | **blocked**: `flute at move 32 strikes a fixture`, `shank at move N strikes a fixture`, `rapid at move N strikes a fixture`, plus `shank/holder ... collides with the part or an island` (722 findings) |
| Vise fitted to the stock (`fit_to_stock: true`, jaw tops Z 38.1) | Z -63.5 | **Z 38.1, the jaw tops** | refused: `Contour: nothing to machine: no material at z = 38.100 - the source spans Z4.000 to Z10.000` | - |
| Vise declared in another setup (`add_setup Setup 2`, vise `setup: Setup 2`), op in the first setup | still the vise base | - | ok | blocked as above |

To confirm the depth, the op was generated with the vise, then the vise was untagged (`remove_fixture`; the op stays `ok`, the model stays) and posted. The post was then refused with `gouge: program cuts below the model in 3920 cell(s), worst 63.50 mm at (-27.31, -27.31, z -99.60)`. The generated path goes to the vise base, Z -99.6.

## Severity

- **The post blocks it** in every case I tried: the fixture collision check catches the flute in the vise. So no gouging G-code was written.
- **It is still wrong output at generate.** Generate reports `ok` with no warning for a path that goes 100 mm into the vise. The only signal is hundreds of verify findings that read as a collision, not "your heights point at the vise".
- In the user's project the workaround was to measure **every** height from Top of Stock.
- The safety still depends on the fixture check catching every case. A fixture tagged in another setup still moves this setup's heights (last row), and the depth comes from steel the op never sees as material.

## Expected

`Top of Model` / `Bottom of Model` are the **part(s)**: the models the op machines (or the setup's non-fixture models). They never include fixtures, accessories, plates, vises, or a stock-source model. A fixture placed in setup B never changes setup A's heights.

**Done means:** with a built-in vise (and an imported fixture) placed, a default 2D Contour on a part resolves Bottom of Model to the part bottom and Top of Model to the part top, in the setup that holds the fixture and in any other setup. A pinning test generates a contour with and without a vise and asserts identical Z levels. The same holds for every kind whose heights default to the model references.

Related: #339 (fixtures/vises), #1094 (a stock-source model judged as a part - the same "which models are the part" question).

What happens: with two setups that both follow the document's post options, a change on Setup2's Post page (`SetPostOptions`, routed by `State::route_post_options` in `crates/ui/src/state_setup_post_options.rs`) writes the DOCUMENT's options whenever Setup2 does not own its options - so Setup1's posted program changes too. Done means: with Setup1 and Setup2 following the document, an options change on Setup2 leaves Setup1's options and the document's unchanged, Setup2 reads the change, undo restores both; single-setup behaviour stated and pinned; the page line names the target.

body:
Reported by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat, on his v0.19.0 build): "Simulator is not updating in realtime - the voxel body updates as the tool comes to the end of a G1 or G2 movement and not while its traveling using a detection of removal/collision whatever we wanna call it.."

Expected: material is removed where the tool is, as it travels. The stock shown at any playback position is the stock cut up to that position (the part of the current move already travelled included), for lines and arcs alike.

Rules:
- Display only: the verdicts (gouge, collision, rapid-in-stock) and what blocks the post must not change. They stay computed over whole moves as today; a partly shown move never hides or delays a finding.
- Scrubbing backwards and jumping in the timeline still show the correct stock for that position.
- Playback stays smooth on a large program (the partial cut of the current move must not re-cut the whole program each frame).

Done means: a test steps playback to the middle of one long G1 and one G2 and reads the stock: material is removed up to the tool position and not beyond it; the end-of-program stock and every verdict are unchanged from before (pinned by the existing sim suites); scrubbing back restores the earlier stock.

body:
Reported by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "you can accidentaly deselect an operations face even when you are on a different tab and working. There is no real "selection" mode that then is locked while you work on the rest of the settings."

What happens: while an operation's dialog is open, a click in the viewport adds or removes geometry from the operation's selection whichever tab is showing (Tool, Heights, Passes, ...). A click meant to orbit, inspect or just focus the viewport silently drops a picked face, and the operation then generates on different geometry.

Expected: picking is a mode. Viewport clicks change the operation's geometry only while the Geometry tab's pick is active (the tab is showing, or its pick row is armed). On every other tab the selection is locked: clicks do not change it, the picked geometry stays highlighted, and the dialog shows plainly whether picking is on or off.

Rules:
- A selection change stays an undoable command (Ctrl+Z restores a face removed by mistake); the lock is ephemeral UI state, not a command.
- With the lock on, a viewport click does nothing to the operation's geometry; it does not fall through to a model or operation selection change that closes or swaps the dialog either.
- Same behaviour for every operation dialog and every pick row (faces, edges, points, entry positions).

Related: issue 1505 (faint edge highlight, sporadic Ctrl/Shift picking) and issue 1507 (hover highlights the selection a row would delete) touch the same pick code.

Done means: a ui harness test opens an operation with a picked face, switches to another tab, clicks the face in the viewport and asserts the selection is unchanged; on the Geometry tab the same click toggles it and undo restores it; the structural test covers the "picking on/off" indication.

title: Edge selection: selected edges are too faint to see, and click / Ctrl / Shift picking is unpredictable (2D Pocket)

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Reported by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat, on v0.19.0, in the 2D Pocket operation): "you cannot really see edge selects the edge gets Purple ish, but its to faint and not marked enough for users to actually see it.. also there is no Ctrl or Shift selection of edges so you can only select one sometimes two, sometimes its the whole chain.. its very sporadic.. this was in the 2D pocket"

What happens:
1. A selected edge is drawn in a faint purple, thin line. On the shaded model it is hard to tell which edges are selected.
2. Picking edges is unpredictable. The page hint says "Ctrl+click adds an edge · Shift+click picks the whole loop", but in 2D Pocket a click sometimes selects one edge, sometimes two, sometimes the whole chain, and Ctrl and Shift do not behave as the hint says.

Expected:
- Selected edges are clearly marked: a thick line in a strong selection colour that stands out on the shaded and the wireframe model in both themes, drawn over the model; the edge under the pointer has its own hover mark before the click.
- One rule for edge picking, the same in every operation that takes edges: click selects that one edge and replaces the selection; Ctrl+click adds or removes one edge; Shift+click selects the whole loop or tangent chain of that edge. The hint text matches what happens.
- The selection list on the Geometry page shows exactly what is selected after each click.

To find first: why the same click gives one edge, two edges or a chain (pick tolerance taking a neighbour edge, automatic chaining, or the modifier keys not reaching the pick), and whether it is 2D Pocket only or every edge-picking operation.

Each selection change goes through the selection command (Everything Is a Command), so undo restores the previous selection.

Found by the review of PR 1464 (the kernel-side `.sc` reader, part of issue 1456).

title: Post-merge test: run the batch gate on the self-hosted Linux runner on every push to main

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the user (2026-11-13, in chat): "Can we setup a build test post merge using local gh runner?"

## Why

AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background" has the main session dispatch a gate-runner agent to run the batch tier on `origin/main` after a fix merges, in the shared main checkout. That costs agent tokens. It blocks the main checkout and any cut meanwhile. It's skipped when a session is busy, so several PRs that were each tested alone merge untested together: today #1432, #1165 and #1181 merged in one batch, after #1405, #1397, #1421 and #1436. The self-hosted Linux runner from #1413 / PR #1418 can run this for free.

## What

A workflow, e.g. `.github/workflows/post-merge.yml`:
- **Trigger:** `push` to `main` only, plus `workflow_dispatch` (input: ref). This is the "user's say-so" AGENTS.md requires for a `push` trigger. Only merged, reviewed code reaches `main`, so no fork can run code on the runner. Never `pull_request` or `pull_request_target`.
- **Runner:** `runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]` (0 billed minutes).
- **Concurrency:** one group for `main` with `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a burst of merges tests only the newest head. The runner is also the cut runner; a cut must not be starved, so say how they share it (e.g. the cut's jobs take priority, or post-merge yields while a `release/*` cut is running).
- **Gate:** `cargo xtask gate batch` (no release-mode heavy lanes; target ≤ 20 min), wrapped in `xvfb-run -a` for the UI suites. Always upload `gate-logs/` as an artifact.
- **On red:** the run fails visibly. Decide how agents and the maintainer hear about it: e.g. the job comments on, or opens, one rolling `main is red` issue (P1, or P0 when it's a G-code test) naming the failing suites and the commit range, and closes it on the next green run. Keep it to one issue, not one per run.
- **Permissions:** `contents: read`, and `issues: write` only on the reporting step.

## Also changes

AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background" (the workflow replaces the gate-runner dispatch; the local batch stays the fallback when the runner is down), and "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted" (a `push` trigger on `main` to the self-hosted runner only). It's a process change, so it bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` and gets announced on #681. A `.github` change gets `needs-maintainer`.

Builds on #1413 (PR #1418, the self-hosted runner and its AGENTS.md section): stack on it, or wait for it to merge.

Done means: a merge to `main` starts the batch gate on the self-hosted runner without anyone dispatching it; a red run tells the agents (the rolling issue); a green run closes that issue; bursts of merges test only the newest head; a cut is never blocked by it; and AGENTS.md says so.

title: Doosan DNM 5700: the optional A states no nose_to_axis, so the index-swing law refuses every program on the built-in, even plain 3-axis work at A0

labels.name: bug

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

Found while fixing #1410. With the DNM travel stated per the travel rule, a plate contour at A0 passes the stroke check, but the post gate still refuses it:

```
2D Contour1: Doosan DNM 5700 turns the work on A but states no nose_to_axis - the tool's clearance over the part swept by the A0.000 index cannot be judged
```

`assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch` declares the catalog's *optional* 4th-axis table (`rot_a`) with no `nose_to_axis`, so `index_swing_problems` (`crates/app/src/posting_index_swing.rs`) refuses every op on this machine. No program posts on the built-in DNM 5700.

## Workaround

State the setup's own `nose_to_axis` (`SetSetupNoseToAxis` / MCP `set_setup_nose_to_axis`), or use another machine.

## Options (pick one; no figure may be invented)

1. State a real `nose_to_axis` for the DNM's rotary, from a published figure for the rotary table the catalog names.
2. Split the file: a plain 3-axis DNM 5700 (no A) and a DNM 5700 + rotary table that carries the figure, or keeps refusing until it is stated.
3. Do not refuse an op whose path never leaves the program's start A when no index happens. This is a change to a safety law, and needs the maintainer.

Done means: a 3-axis face job on a built-in DNM 5700 machine posts, and the rotary variant still refuses an unjudgeable index by name. Pinned in `crates/app/tests/vmc_stroke.rs` (`a_plate_contour_on_the_built_in_dnm_passes_the_stroke` currently asserts that this is the only refusal).

title: Process: a P1/P2 issue filed after a cut has started does not restart the cut

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:low
labels.description: Mechanical, one file, no new logic (issue-worker-low)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat, after the v0.19.0 cut): "We should as a rule not let P1/P2s coming in after cut - force a restart as its a ~2 hour job".

## What happened

AGENTS.md says "A minor/major cut does not start while any `P1` or `P2` issue is open". During the v0.19.0 cut two such issues were filed after the release branch existed (issue 1417, P1, a red xtask unit test; issue 1398, P2, the Fanuc lathe live-tool feed cap). Fixing them in the cut means merging to main, merging main into the release branch and running the release gate again, about 50 minutes of gate and about two hours in all. The maintainer decided in the question dialog: "Tag now as it is"; both were named as known issues on the release PR.

## What to change (AGENTS.md, "Priorities" and "Commits and Releases")

- The `P1`/`P2` rule is a start condition: it is checked once, when the cut starts (step 1). The session records the time and the list of open `P1`/`P2` issues (none) in the release PR body.
- A `P1` or `P2` issue filed after that moment does not restart the cut and is not merged into it. The cut finishes on the tree that passed the release gate. Each such issue is named under "Known issues" in the release notes on the GitHub release and in a comment on the release PR, and its fix merges after the tag and ships in the next minor.
- The maintainer can still stop a cut by saying so; no agent stops or restarts one for a late issue. An agent that finds a late `P1` (unsafe or wrong output) tells the maintainer in one line and goes on.
- Failures of the cut's own release gate are different: they are what the gate is for, and are still fixed in the cut as today.
- Update the `merge-ready` skill's precondition text and the release steps where they repeat the rule.

Process files change: bump `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, add a `docs/decisions/` entry quoting the maintainer, announce on issue 681 when it merges.

Done means: AGENTS.md states the start-condition reading and the known-issues step, the skills that repeat the rule agree with it, `PROCESS_VERSION` is bumped, and nothing in the text lets an agent restart a cut for an issue filed after its start.

title: PR test pipeline on the self-hosted runner: the PR-reviewer hands the build and tests to GitHub Actions when a runner is online

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "there should be an agent change and prob pr-reviewer change that when the pr-review is done instead of doing the build locally, we check if there is hosted github runners present and push the testing as PR build to the github actions self hosted runner... Which means prob both the pr-reviewer skill need or just the skill need to be able to determine that and the testing pipeline needs to be created."

Related: issue 1413 (cut pipeline, Linux, self-hosted runners only), issue 1415 / PR 1416 (removes the unused `ci.yml` and `nightly.yml`).

## Why

Every PR review builds the workspace and runs the touched suites in a worktree on the reviewer's machine: 10-20 GB of `target/` each, up to four at once, competing with gates and cuts for the same machine.

## What

1. **A PR test workflow** (here `pr-test.yml`) for the self-hosted Linux runner (`runs-on: [self-hosted, linux]`): input is a PR number; it trial-merges the PR head with current main, builds, runs `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` (the suites the diff touches) and clippy for the touched crates, and reports pass/fail per binary with the failing output.
2. **Runner detection.** Before building, the reviewer asks whether a self-hosted runner is online (`gh api repos/NeoTech/Camcraft/actions/runners --jq '.runners[] | select(.status=="online")'`). Online: start the workflow for the PR (`gh workflow run pr-test.yml -f pr=<N>`), wait for the run (`gh run watch`), and read its result and logs into the review. None online, or the run cannot start: build locally as today. The review comment says which of the two ran, with the run's link.
3. **Where the logic lives.** In the `review-prs` skill and the `PR-reviewer` agent definition (`.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`); decide whether detection sits in the skill (the dispatcher starts the run, the reviewer reads it) or in the agent. The reviewer still reads the diff, checks AGENTS.md's laws and writes the review itself; only the build and test step moves.

## Open questions (decide before code)

- **Trigger and safety.** A self-hosted runner executes the PR's code (build scripts, tests) on the maintainer's hardware. AGENTS.md says "Never add a `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger without the user's say-so". Proposed: `workflow_dispatch` only, started by a collaborator's session, so a fork PR can never start a run by itself; the job gets no secrets and a read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN`; the runner works in a clean checkout per run. A `pull_request` trigger for PRs from collaborators' own branches is the alternative, and needs the maintainer's explicit yes.
- **`needs-maintainer` PRs.** Today a PR with a new dependency or a `build.rs` / scripts / `.github` change is read, not built. That rule should hold on the runner too.
- **Linux only.** Windows-only readings (per-OS pinned values, the Windows arm of issue 1402) are not checked by a Linux run; say whether the reviewer still runs those locally when the diff touches them.
- **Concurrency.** One runner, up to four reviews: a queue (`concurrency:` per PR), and what the reviewer does while it waits.
- **UI tests.** The ui suites spawn the real app through the test harness; say whether the runner can run them headless or they stay local.
- **Fallback truthfulness.** A run that is cancelled or times out is not a pass: the reviewer falls back to the local build or reports "not built".

## Also changes

`.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`, `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md` and AGENTS.md ("Outside PRs are reviewed", "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted") are process files: the PR bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` and is announced on issue 681. A `.github` change is read by the maintainer before it merges.

Done means: with the runner online, a review of a test PR starts the workflow, the review comment carries the run's link and per-binary result, and no local build ran; with the runner offline, the same review builds locally as today; a fork PR cannot start the workflow by itself; AGENTS.md and the runner setup notes describe it.

title: Cut pipeline on GitHub Actions: build and test the cut on GitHub, then run the release pipeline for the tag

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P4
labels.description: Work the maintainer asked for, for the next cut

body:
Asked for by the maintainer (2026-11-13, in chat): "We need an issue for a "Cut" pipeline on Github Actions that will be building and testing the cut on github rather than locally. And when that is done it will run the Release pipeline for that tagged version."

## Why

The v0.19.0 cut ran the release gate tier locally in the main checkout: about 75 minutes per run, three runs (two red, one after the fixes), with the checkout and the machine blocked for every other session meanwhile. Suites that only run in the release tier (kernel STEP agreement, the app heavy lane, the UI snapshot lane) went red only at the cut.

## What

A manually started workflow (`workflow_dispatch`, input: the version), here called `cut.yml`, that takes a `release/vX.Y.0` branch and:

1. builds it and runs the release gate tier on GitHub (`cargo xtask gate release`, or the same lanes split into jobs);
2. on green, makes the cut's tag on the release merge commit and starts the existing release pipeline (`release.yml`) for that tag; on red, tags nothing and reports the failing lanes.

## Open questions (decide before code)

- **Actions budget.** AGENTS.md budgets 3000 minutes a month, Windows billed 2x, macOS 10x, and says "Never add a `push`, `pull_request` or `schedule` trigger without the user's say-so". The local release gate is about 75 minutes on a warm cache; a cold Windows runner will be slower and bills double. Which OS runs the gate (Linux only, or Windows too because the pinned move counts differ per OS, issue 1402)? What caching (sccache, `Swatinem/rust-cache`)?
- **Where the tag is made.** Today step 4 tags the release PR's merge commit by hand after `git diff $tip $m` is empty. Does the workflow run before the release PR merges (on the branch) and tag after the merge, or run on main after the merge? A tag pushed with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` does not trigger `release.yml`; the workflow has to call it (`workflow_call`) or use another token.
- **Snapshot goldens.** They are regenerated at the cut after a human look at the `.diff.png` files. The workflow needs to hand those files over (artifact upload) and wait, or the regeneration stays a local step before the workflow starts.
- **Version bump, zip and installer.** `cargo xtask release --no-tag --installer` does these locally today; `release.yml` builds the published artifact. Say which of them move.
- **What stays local.** The quick and batch tiers are not part of this issue.

## Also changes

AGENTS.md "Commits and Releases" (the cut steps) and "GitHub Actions minutes are budgeted" describe the local cut; a PR for this changes them, bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` and is announced on the pinned issue 681. A `.github` change is read by the maintainer before it merges (`needs-maintainer`).

Done means: a cut of a test version on a scratch branch runs the gate on GitHub from one manual start, a red gate makes no tag, a green one ends with the release pipeline's artifact attached to the GitHub release for that tag, and AGENTS.md describes the new steps with the billed minutes of one cut measured and written down.

title: Land model: stepped lids churn a retract-and-plunge at every lid step edge

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## The churn, root-caused

Follow-up to #1286 (the land model), picking up the finding from my review of that PR: on a part whose surface is not flat, the path fragments around the lids — every crossing of a filled hole costs a retract → rapid → plunge every ~0.5–1 mm instead of one continuous lateral bridge.

The cause is downstream of the fill rule itself: **the closing levels a lid's cells a hair apart, and `emit` gives each cell its own height, so the lid is a staircase.** At each step edge the ball can seat on neither plane for a full ball-width annulus — the higher lid top blocks it from seating on the lower, and a lid top's free edge carries no fold support (lids are horizontal tops-only quads). Support goes `None` across that annulus, and the march retracts and plunges at every step.

Repro: the #1196 part (4B52391, two stepped through-holes, roof descending ~0.04 mm per 1.06 mm grid cell across hole 1). `fill_openings(width = 12.7, tol = 0.01)`, then `parallel` with `stepover 0.6`, ball Ø6, `tol 0.05`, `clearance_z 30`. Vertical feed moves near the hole centers:

| | fill off | fill on (current) | fill on (fixed) |
|---|---|---|---|
| near the holes | 22 | 166 | 40 |
| elsewhere | 36 | 128 | 57 |

(The `fill off` path is byte-identical baseline; the fix cuts the lid-induced plunges by ~75%.)

## The fix

One plane per opening: before emitting, lift the whole lid — the raised component **and** its one-cell ring — to the highest closed height over all of those cells (`Grid::plateau` in `fill.rs`). The plateau runs *after* the `enclosed` check, so enclosure is still judged against the closing's own levels. Doc-law updated: "One plane per opening" now covers the ring cells.

Regression test: `a_pocket_under_a_descending_roof_gets_one_flat_lid` in `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_land.rs` — a pocket under a shallow descending roof must come out coplanar, and the land never descends into the pocket.

## Bounded residuals (documented, not solved here)

Two narrow `None` zones remain at the lid/model boundary on the repro part, both inherent to tops-only lids:

- west rim: x ∈ [25.17, 25.40], **0.23 mm** — free-edge seating artifact where the lid is flush with the roof (7.085 vs 7.0848);
- east rim: x ∈ [31.76, 33.23], **1.47 mm** — the roof descends eastward (~0.27 mm drop to the ring's last cell), and a flat lid over a sloping roof always steps down to the real surface at its edge.

Both are ball-seating artifacts at the step, not interior churn. A follow-up giving lids side faces (or edge support at lid boundaries) could close them; I'm leaving that out of this fix since each residual is bounded and at most one extra plunge per rim crossing.

Also out of scope here: the V-crease being treated as a third opening (the depth-guard idea from the #1286 review) — that stays separate.

title: Mazak post writes the spindle start and stop as MOTON S.. / MOTOFF - not ISO 6983 words, no direction before a G84; which Mazak document gives them?

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: P1
labels.description: Unsafe or wrong output: gouge, collision, wrong G-code, crash, data loss; blocks a cut

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

body:
## What happens

The Mazak post starts and stops the spindle with `MOTON S..` and `MOTOFF` in every section:

```
T2 M6
G43 H2
MOTON S600
M8
G00 X0 Y0 Z20
G99
G84 X0 Y0 Z8 R20 F600
G80
G00 X0 Y0 Z45
M9
MOTOFF
```

These are the only multi-letter words in the program. The post's own header gives its grammar as "public RS-274/ISO 6983 documentation". In that grammar a word is an address letter followed by a number (`M3`, `S600`), so `MOTON` and `MOTOFF` are not words of it.

`MOTON` also states no direction. The block after it is a right-hand rigid tap (`G84`), which needs the spindle turning clockwise.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`assets/posts/mazak.cps` is unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

The part is a Ø36 × 20 disc with a Ø5 blind hole to z 4. On the built-in `VMC 3-axis`:

- **D1:** Drill with `cycle: "peck"`, `peck: 2`.
- **D2:** Drill with `cycle: "drill"`, `dwell: 0.5`.
- **T1:** Drill with `TAP-M6`, `cycle: "tap"`, threaded to z 8.

`generate` and `verify` are clean. `post` with `"post": "Mazak"` writes 49 lines, with `MOTON S7500` / `MOTON S600` and `MOTOFF` around each section as above. The words have been in the post since it shipped (4288300f, M3.3 B), and the goldens under `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/mazak/` lock them.

## Neighbour case

The same stream through the other Fanuc-family posts (`Fanuc`, `Haas`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `tormach.cps`) writes `S600 M3` before the tap and `M5` at section end.

## Root cause (unknown)

The header credits the words to "the control family's published operator conventions" ("spindle-logic M words MOTON/MOTOFF with the speed on the same block"), but names no document. I found no public Mazak EIA/ISO material that uses them. If a Mazak control does not accept them, every program from this post fails at its first spindle start. That is either an alarm, or feeds with the spindle stopped if the block is skipped.

Which published Mazak document gives `MOTON` / `MOTOFF` as the spindle start and stop words?

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P1` if the words are not Mazak's (wrong posted G-code in every Mazak program). The question above settles that.
- `effort:high`: posted G-code.
- `area:post`
