title: Doosan DNM 5700 machine states Z travel -510..0 (machine frame): every move above the work origin is refused at the post, as in #457

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

On the built-in **Doosan DNM 5700** machine, the post gate refuses every move above the work origin's Z0: every clearance, retract and cut above the origin. The cause is that its Z travel is stated in the machine frame. A plain face job's first rapid already fails:

```
post: post blocked - machine Doosan DNM 5700: 40 limit problem(s): F1: move 0 reaches 35.000 in Z, the stroke is -510.000..0.000; F1: move 1 reaches 10.000 in Z, the stroke is -510.000..0.000; ...
```

This is the #457 defect, which `vmc.mch` and `tilthead.mch` were fixed for, in the machine registered later by #614.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`assets/machines/doosan-dnm.mch` and `crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs` are unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

```json
[["load_machine", {"builtin": "Doosan DNM 5700"}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 60, "dy": 40, "dz": 10}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-1000-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "face", "tool": "EM-1000-4FL", "name": "F1"}],
 ["generate", {"name": "F1"}], ["verify", {}],
 ["post", {"output": "f1.nc", "post": "Doosan DNM"}]]
```

`verify` returns one `post_gate` finding (`blocks_post: true`) with the 40 limit problems, and `post` refuses with them as quoted above.

## Neighbour case that works

The same calls with `{"builtin": "VMC 3-axis"}` and the `Fanuc` post: `verify` is clean, and the post writes 40 lines (`G00 X-35 Y-15 Z35`, `G01 ... Z10 F300`, ...). The program is the same; only the machine's stated bands differ.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (the `travel` bullet) says:

> a stroke in PROGRAM coordinates ... The file cannot know the work offset, so a linear slide of stroke L is written `-L..L` - the FULL stroke each way, never the machine-frame band (`-500..0` for a 500 mm column refuses every retract above the work origin, #457 ...)

`doosan-dnm.mch` states:

- **Z:** `{ "min": -510.0, "max": 0.0 }`, the machine-frame band. The limit check (`crates/app/src/machine/mod.rs`, the travel loop) reads `(w - origin) * sign` against it, so every move above the work origin fails.
- **X and Y:** `-510..510` and `-285..285`, half the catalog strokes in the file's own description ("X/Y/Z: 1020/570/510mm"). The rule's full-stroke-each-way form is `-1020..1020` and `-570..570`. As stated, a program whose work origin sits at a table corner is refused once it runs past 510 mm in X or 285 mm in Y.

Every other shipped mill file states a symmetric Z band (`vmc.mch` and `tilthead.mch` ±500, `grblhal-3axis.mch` ±100, the Tormach, Sienci and Carvera files ± their figures). `load_machine` derives the table from the same numbers: `"table": {"max": [510.0, 285.0, -510.0], ...}`.

## Expected

The DNM file follows the travel rule: `-1020..1020`, `-570..570` and `-510..510`. The face job posts as it does on the built-in VMC. A test like `crates/app/tests/vmc_stroke.rs` (#477) pins it.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a legal program on a shipped machine is refused. Another machine is the only workaround.
- `effort:high`: the fix is a data change plus a pinning test, but it moves the travel and collision laws, so the safety floor applies.
- `area:post`
- `source:agent`

title: A new lathe Facing faces the part away: the seed's facing plane is Bottom of Model and its top is Top of Model, so the stock allowance is never faced

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A lathe Facing created with its seed heights faces the part away down to its bottom, and leaves the stock allowance above the part untouched. The seed sets:

- `top_z` to Top of Model.
- `bottom_z`, the finished facing plane, to Bottom of Model.

The MCP `add_operation` creates from `operation::seed_params` (#511). The GUI's quick-add (`quick_params`) retypes the same Face draft, so it gets the same heights. Only the MCP path was run.

`generate` says `ok`. `verify` holds the post, but its words understate the cut: "0.8000 mm gouge" for passes that cut 48 mm into the part.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/seed.rs` and `crates/motion/src/turning/face.rs` are unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

The part is a plain bar, r 10 from z 0 to 48: an ASCII STL revolved from the meridian `(0,0) (10,0) (10,48) (0,48)` with 64 segments. The stock is a cylinder of 20 × 50, so 2 mm of facing allowance stands above the part.

```json
[["load_machine", {"path": "assets/machines/lathe.mch"}],
 ["import_model", {"path": "cyl.stl"}],
 ["set_stock", {"cylinder": {"diameter": 20, "height": 50}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "TN-1600-0R8"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "facing", "tool": "TN-1600-0R8", "name": "F1", "source": "cyl"}],
 ["generate", {"name": "F1"}], ["verify", {}],
 ["post", {"output": "f1.nc", "post": "assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps"}]]
```

- `get_job` shows the seed: `"top_z": {"offset": 0.0, "reference": "top_of_model"}, "bottom_z": {"offset": 0.0, "reference": "bottom_of_model"}`.
- `generate` returns `status: ok` with 487 moves. That is 97 stations at the 0.5 stepdown, from z 0 up to z 48.
- `verify` returns:
  ```
  finish envelope near move 3: 0.8000 mm gouge, 0.0092 mm rest
  rapid move 4 travels below the clearance plane inside stock
  rapid move 5 travels below the clearance plane inside stock
  ```
- `post` is refused: `post blocked - 3 warning(s): ...`

## Neighbour case that works

On the same document, `edit_operation` with `top_z` = Top of Stock and `bottom_z` = Top of Model gives 27 moves and no findings. It posts 42 lines: five passes `X-1.6` at Z50, Z49.5, Z49, Z48.5 and Z48.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`seed_facing` (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`) takes `top: c.top` and `bottom: c.bottom` from `Carried::of` the seed Face. Face has neither field, so the fold's defaults fill them: `Height::of(TopOfModel, 0.0)` and `Height::of(BottomOfModel, 0.0)`. The second is the #214 choice ("the part's own floor") made for the mill kinds' depth.

For Facing that floor becomes the facing plane. `turning::facing` then ladders from `facing_z` = 0 up to `min(top_z, z_top)` = 48, so the allowance above 48 is never reached and every station below it cuts the part.

`seed_facing` already overrides the fold's stepdown for this family ("the mill default the fold carries would refuse against the house insert's 0.8 mm nose"). The heights get no such override. The test `the_facing_seed_faces_the_bar` (`crates/app/tests/turning.rs`) passes `top` and `bottom` as fixed 16 and 14 in a hand-built `Carried`, so it never meets the fold's defaults.

On the verify wording: `EnvelopeReport::gouge_mm` saturates at the ball radius by design ("a path that buried its centers in material reads the saturation value `r`"). So the reported 0.8 mm is the nose radius, not the depth cut.

## Expected

A new Facing faces the allowance down to the part's top: Top of Stock down to Top of Model, the heights of the neighbour case. When the part is already at length, it says there is nothing to face.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: every new Facing cuts the part away until its heights are edited. The gate catches it, so it is not P1.
- `effort:high`: a small diff (one seed in `kinds.rs`, plus a test that runs `seed_params` itself), but it changes what a new op posts, so the safety floor applies.
- `area:turning`
- `source:agent`

title: Lathe Facing on a grooved bar is refused at the post: the sphere-envelope scan counts the groove floor across the spindle as rest

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

A lathe Facing that only faces the end of a bar is refused at the post when the bar has a groove anywhere along it. The same Facing on a plain or stepped bar posts. `verify` reports the groove as unremoved rest belonging to the Facing:

```
F2: finish envelope near move 3: 0.0000 mm gouge, 17.0528 mm rest   (blocks_post: true)
post: post blocked - 1 warning(s): F2: finish envelope near move 3: 0.0000 mm gouge, 15.5616 mm rest
```

The groove lies 11 mm below the faced band. No Facing can reach it, and the Groove kinds exist to cut it.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`crates/sim/src/verify/finish.rs`, `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/`, `crates/motion/src/turning/` and `crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs` are unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

The bars are closed revolves about Z with 64 segments, written as ASCII STL from a meridian of (r, z) points:

- **plain:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,48) (0,48)`
- **stepped:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,20) (7,20) (7,40) (5,40) (5,48) (0,48)`
- **wider at the free end:** `(0,0) (7,0) (7,20) (10,20) (10,48) (0,48)`
- **groove:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,34) (5.5,34) (5.5,37) (10,37) (10,48) (0,48)`
- **groove near the top:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,44) (8,44) (8,46) (10,46) (10,48) (0,48)`
- **shaft:** `(0,0) (10,0) (10,20) (7,20) (7,34) (5.5,34) (5.5,37) (7,37) (7,40) (5,40) (5,48) (0,48)`

```json
[["load_machine", {"path": "assets/machines/lathe.mch"}],
 ["import_model", {"path": "<bar>.stl"}],
 ["set_stock", {"cylinder": {"diameter": 20, "height": 50}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "TN-1600-0R8"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "facing", "tool": "TN-1600-0R8", "name": "F2", "source": "<bar>",
   "params": {"top_z": {"offset": 0, "reference": "top_of_stock"}, "bottom_z": {"offset": 0, "reference": "top_of_model"}}}],
 ["generate", {"name": "F2"}], ["verify", {}],
 ["post", {"output": "f2.nc", "post": "assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps"}]]
```

The Facing generates 27 moves on each bar: five stations from z 50 down to z 48.

| Bar | `verify` | Post |
|---|---|---|
| plain | no findings | written (42 lines) |
| stepped | no findings | written (with Profile Rough + Finish: 829 lines) |
| wider at the free end | no findings | - |
| groove | `0.0000 mm gouge, 17.0528 mm rest` | blocked |
| groove near the top | `0.0000 mm gouge, 10.2818 mm rest` | blocked |
| shaft | `0.0000 mm gouge, 15.5616 mm rest` | blocked |

## Root cause (confirmed)

Facing's registry row is `mode: Mode::Envelope` (`crates/app/src/operation/kinds.rs`, Facing `KindInfo`). Its comment reads: "a meridian circle revolved IS a sphere about the axis, so the scan reads the lathe's own cut". `finish_envelope` (`crates/sim/src/verify/finish.rs`) then runs `stock_sim::envelope_scan_centers` over the pass as it lies in world space, a radial line in the y = 0 half-plane x ≥ 0. The scan never turns the work.

The scan's `rest_mm` includes "material standing hidden under an occluding top" (M2.2d, `EnvelopeReport::rest_mm` in `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/scan.rs`). A groove's floor is an upward face under the bar's full diameter above it, so it counts. Every reported figure equals the distance from the groove floor's outer rim on the far side of the axis (x = −r_rim, y = 0, z = floor) to the last pass's nose centre at the axis (0, 0, 48 + 0.8), less the 0.8 nose:

| Bar | Floor rim | √(r_rim² + (48.8 − z_floor)²) − 0.8 | Reported |
|---|---|---|---|
| groove | r 10, z 34 | 17.06 | 17.0528 |
| groove near the top | r 10, z 44 | 10.29 | 10.2818 |
| shaft | r 7, z 34 | 15.57 | 15.5616 |

The figures sit slightly below the true-circle values because the 64-gon floor rim is a chord.

The Groove rows of the same table already say why a sphere scan cannot judge this ("No sphere can judge a band: a grooved part is undercut BY DESIGN"), and they use `Mode::Revolve`.

Seen on the same shaft, but not root-caused: Profile Rough and Profile Finish (also `Mode::Envelope`) report `12.7553 mm rest` and `0.0073 mm gouge, 12.4890 mm rest` with default heights. A stepped bar without a groove gives them no findings.

## Expected

A Facing is judged on the band it claims, as the turned work sees it. A groove elsewhere on the bar is not its rest, and the program posts as it does on a bar without the groove.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a legal turning program is refused.
- `effort:high`: verifier logic; the safety floor.
- `area:turning`
- `source:agent`

title: 3D Finish and 3D Pocket refuse the sample STEP laid flat: two solids sharing a face slice as "non-manifold contact", reported as invalid machining parameters

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:3d
labels.description: 3D milling and finishing

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
## What happens

`testdata/models/sample_ap214.step` laid flat (rotated -90° about X) cannot be machined by any 3D operation. 3D Finish and 3D Pocket are both refused before any toolpath is planned:

```
generate: S1 - could not generate the toolpath: S1: invalid machining parameters: chords meet 3+ ways at z = 1.8359437500001423: non-manifold contact
generate: R1 - could not generate the toolpath: R1: invalid machining parameters: chords meet 3+ ways at z = 1.8359437500001423: non-manifold contact
```

The model is a valid STEP file. The message blames "machining parameters", but no parameter is at fault, and nothing tells the user what is wrong with the model or what to change.

## Reproduction (main 38699549, `camcraft-cli mcp`)

`slice.rs`, `slice_weld.rs`, `crates/app/src/operation/` and `crates/motion/src/machining3d/` are unchanged from there to 3f6ecb4a.

```json
[["import_model", {"path": "testdata/models/sample_ap214.step"}],
 ["move_model", {"name": "sample_ap214", "position": [0, -26.7192, 1.5875], "rotation": [-0.7071067811865476, 0, 0, 0.7071067811865476]}],
 ["set_stock", {"box": {"dx": 70, "dy": 124, "dz": 8}}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "BN-0600"}],
 ["add_tool", {"catalog": "EM-0600-4FL"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "finish3d", "tool": "BN-0600", "name": "S1", "source": "sample_ap214"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "pocket3d", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "R1", "source": "sample_ap214"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "contour", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "C1", "source": "sample_ap214"}],
 ["add_operation", {"kind": "pocket", "tool": "EM-0600-4FL", "name": "P1", "source": "sample_ap214"}],
 ["generate", {"name": "S1"}], ["generate", {"name": "R1"}],
 ["generate", {"name": "C1"}], ["generate", {"name": "P1"}]]
```

S1 and R1 are refused as quoted above. The Parallel and Waterline patterns of 3D Finish give the same refusal.

## Neighbour cases that work

- The same model in the same placement, with 2D Contour C1 and 2D Pocket P1: both generate (`status: ok`, 52 and 748 moves).
- A throwaway test called `geometry::slice::slice` on `model::world_facets` of the laid-flat model, every 0.05 mm in Z. The model is three solids (`MANIFOLD_SOLID_BREP` 'Part 1' to 'Part 3'). It was split into bodies by shared vertices:

| Facets sliced | Z span (mm) | Planes refused |
|---|---|---|
| all three solids | 0 .. 6.5278 | 32 of 129 (z 1.60 .. 3.15) |
| body 0 alone (1758 facets) | 0 .. 3.1750 | 0 of 62 |
| body 1 alone (968 facets) | 1.5875 .. 4.7625 | 0 of 62 |
| body 2 alone (452 facets) | 0.1778 .. 6.5278 | 0 of 126 |
| bodies 0 + 1 | 0 .. 4.7625 | 32 of 94 (z 1.60 .. 3.15) |
| bodies 0 + 2 | 0 .. 6.5278 | 0 of 129 |
| bodies 1 + 2 | 0.1778 .. 6.5278 | 0 of 126 |
| all three, as imported (not rotated) | -32.357 .. 85.851 | 0 of 2363 |

The refused band is exactly where bodies 0 and 1 overlap in Z: 1.5875 .. 3.175.

## Root cause (confirmed)

`slice()` in `crates/geometry/src/geometry/slice.rs` (step 2, lines 158-180) requires every chord end to be shared by exactly two chords. Bodies 0 and 1 share a cylindrical face of radius 17.5146 mm about the model's XY origin (0, -26.7192), and both solids carry identical tessellation vertices on it. Laid flat, that face stands vertical. Every plane through the two bodies' common height therefore cuts both section outlines through the same points. At z = 2.0 there are 93 such points, all at r = 17.5146, each the end of four chords (two from each body). The exact weld returns `SliceError::NonManifold` there.

That refusal comes before step 4 (`Region::from_slices`), whose comment reads "the non-zero fuse unites shells". As imported, the cylinder's axis is horizontal, and every plane slices (last row of the table).

`from_slice` in `crates/app/src/operation/material.rs:250` and `crates/motion/src/machining3d/rest.rs:23` then maps the refusal to `GenError::Invalid`. That error prints as "invalid machining parameters: …".

### Related

M13.11 already reads a plane as the union of touching bodies, but only for a selection across several models:

- `Material.bodies` (`crates/app/src/operation/material.rs`) is filled only in `material_of`'s `SrcRef::Selection` arm.
- `verify::verify_bodies` and `machining2d::contour_on_bodies` read it.

A single model holding several solids arrives as `SrcRef::Entity`, so `bodies` stays empty. `material::section()` then slices its facets plainly.

## Expected

Solids of one model that touch along a face slice as their union; each solid slices on its own at every one of those planes. If a section really cannot be built, the refusal names the model and says its solids touch at that height, instead of blaming machining parameters.

## Suggested labels

Outside contributors can't set labels, so these are suggestions:

- `P3`: a legal 3D job on a shipped sample model is refused, with a misleading message.
- `effort:high`: slicer behaviour; the geometry safety floor.
- `area:3d`
- `source:agent`

body:
**What happens.** `explain()` (`crates/post/src/post/explain.rs`, from #1394) explains every post's words from one table, `_EXPLAIN_WORDS`, keyed by the word alone. Two shipped lathe posts write words that mean something else on their control:

- `fanuc-lathe.cps` writes `G99` as feed per revolution (`onOpen`, line 368: `// unit, ZX plane, no nose comp, feed/rev`) and `G98` as feed per minute (C-axis live tooling, line 553). The table says G98 = `CYCLE RETURNS TO START HEIGHT`, G99 = `CYCLE RETURNS TO R HEIGHT`.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` (line 428) and `tormach-lathe.cps` (line 383) write `T0101`: tool/station 1, offset 1. `_explainWord` reads the whole number: `TOOL 101`.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` writes `G50 S<rpm>` as the spindle speed clamp (lines 432, 445, 458). G50 is not in the table, so the block is explained as `SPEED 3000` alone, which reads as a speed command.

**Reproduction** (main `38699549`). A test post that declares `explains = "paren"` and whose `block()` appends `explain(words)` (the shape `crates/post/tests/explain.rs` uses) was fed the blocks fanuc-lathe writes and posted through `engine::run_with` with `{"Explain": true}`:

```
G21 G18 G40 G80 G99 (MM UNITS, XZ PLANE, RADIUS COMP CANCEL, CANCEL DRILL CYCLE)
T0101 (TOOL 101)
G50 S3000 (SPEED 3000)
G96 S200 M3 (CONSTANT SURFACE SPEED, SPEED 200, SPINDLE ON CLOCKWISE)
G98 (CYCLE RETURNS TO START HEIGHT)
G99 (CYCLE RETURNS TO R HEIGHT)
G95 (FEED PER REVOLUTION)
G76 P010060 Q50 R0.02 (THREADING CYCLE)
```

Neighbour cases that read right: `G95` (tormach-lathe's feed per revolution) and `G76` (both lathes' threading cycle). On the mill posts `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps`, G99 does mean the R-plane return (#994).

**Reach today.** No shipped post declares `explains` yet, so no posted program carries these comments. #1388 names `fanuc-lathe.cps` and #1387 names `tormach-lathe.cps` among the posts that opt in next, so they would be the first to write them.

**Root cause (confirmed):** the meanings are one table keyed by word, with no way for a post to say what a word means on its control. The #1386 decision file sources the wording from RS-274 / ISO 6983 and the LinuxCNC lists, where G98/G99 are the canned-cycle returns. `_explainWord` also reads a `T` word as a single number.

**Done means:** a lathe post that opts into Explain never writes a mill meaning for G98/G99, never reads T0101 as tool 101, and never presents `G50 S` as a plain speed. One way: a post states its own meanings for the words its control reads differently, or the words to leave unexplained. Pin it with a test that posts G98, G99, G50 S and T0101 through fanuc-lathe with Explain on.

Suggested labels (an outside contributor cannot set them): `P7` while no lathe post explains (it becomes a misleading comment, `P3`, once #1387 or #1388 wires one), `effort:medium`, `area:post`, `source:agent`.

body:
Found while refreshing PR #1136 (#543, sinker rough and finish with undersize) over main's #544 (sinker orbit).

What happens now: #543's size law (`motion::sinker_undersize::judge`) sizes a rough or finish burn as electrode + 2 x spark gap per axis, and places the tip one undersize above the finished floor. #544's orbit moves the electrode a further `radius` sideways at the burn floor, so an orbited pass burns electrode + 2 x (gap + radius) wide. The law does not count that, so PR #1136 refuses an orbit on a rough or finish by name (`SinkerBurnOp::pass_refusal`, at command creation and at generate) instead of judging it wrongly. A plain single burn may still orbit.

What should happen: the common practice is that the electrode undersize per side covers gap + orbit, so a finish with an orbit should be judged as `e + 2(g + r) == c` (a rough: `<= c`), with the floor stand worked out so the floor is neither left short nor over-burned by the orbit, and the stock-sim verdict pinning both.

Done means: a Sinker Burn rough or finish accepts an orbit; `judge` counts the radius in the burned width; a finish with an orbit burns the cavity to size (sim verdict clean, 0 gouge, rest within the sim's resolution); an orbit that would push the walls past the cavity is refused by name; the refusal added in PR #1136 is removed; pins in `sinker_undersize` cover both.

body:
Found while working #31 (PR #1314) on macOS.

What happens: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` stops on a stock Mac for two reasons.
- It calls `sed -i` in GNU form (no suffix argument). BSD sed reads the next argument as the backup suffix and fails or edits the wrong thing.
- Line ~104 expands `"${PROFILE_ARGS[@]}"` while the array is empty under `set -u`. bash 3.2, the macOS `/bin/bash`, treats that as an unbound variable and exits.

Done means: `web/build-app-wasm.sh` and `web/check-app-page.sh` run unmodified on macOS with /bin/bash and BSD sed.

title: Process: every open process PR conflicts on .claude/PROCESS_VERSION each time another one merges

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:medium
labels.description: One module or crate, a known pattern (issue-worker-medium)

labels.name: P7
labels.description: Owed polish and small fixes

body:
Seen on 2026-11-12, a day with about 50 merges: `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one integer that every process PR increments in its own branch. Each time one of them merges, every other open process PR either conflicts on that one line (GitHub shows CONFLICTING and the PR drops out of a merge run) or, worse, carries the SAME new number and merges cleanly - two process changes then share one number and a fork that already synced at it never pulls the second (it happened with #1117 and #930 at 17; fixed by the extra bump PR #1142). Today #965, #967, #972, #1033, #1024, #1100, #1116 and #1151 all had to be renumbered by hand, some more than once.

The law today (AGENTS.md "Process changes bump PROCESS_VERSION"): the PR increments the number; "whichever merges second takes the next number when it merges main".

Proposal to decide (maintainer): the number is not written in the PR at all. A process PR only says in its body "process change: yes" (the reviewer checks that instead of the bump); the merging session increments `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` right after the merge in a one-line follow-up PR (or the merge tooling does: `cargo xtask process-bump`), and posts the #681 announcement with that number. One writer, no conflicts, no shared numbers. Alternatives: derive the version from the count of merge commits touching the process paths (no file at all), or keep the file and make `.gitattributes` resolve it with a custom "max + 1" merge driver (needs local git config on every clone, so probably not).

Done means: the chosen rule is in AGENTS.md (and the review-prs / merge-ready skills), two process PRs open at once no longer conflict with each other, and two of them can never land on the same number; `PROCESS_VERSION` bumped and announced for this change itself.

title: Work offsets: core uses an index, the post supplies the word and display name

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:post
labels.description: Post processors and G-code

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: area:mcp
labels.description: MCP server and agent tooling (crates/app/src/mcp, camcraft-mcp skill)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
## Problem

A setup stores its work offset as an index (`SetupDef::work_offset`), but core
turns that index into a Fanuc-style word before any post is involved:

- The table `WCS_SLOTS = ["G54".."G59"]` lives in `camcraft-app`
  (`operation/types/sel.rs`) and is read directly by the Setups page combo,
  `setup::wcs_label`, the setup sheet, the MCP `set_work_offset` tool and the
  refusal messages.
- `posting::wcs_context` writes the word, not the index, into the stream as
  `PARAM WorkOffset`. Posts then parse it back: Fanuc and Mazak use
  `slotOf("G55") -> 1`, Heidenhain regex-matches `^G5([4-9])$` to pick a preset
  row.
- An index of 6 or more is refused in core, so extended offsets
  (`G54.1 P..`, Sinumerik `G505+`, further Heidenhain preset rows) cannot be
  expressed.

A setup with no machine and no post still shows `G54`: the word comes from
neither. Every other ask in the stream is already dialect-neutral (coolant,
after-operation); the work offset is the exception.

## Proposal

1. **Stream carries the index.** `PARAM WorkOffset` becomes a 1-based number.
   A manifest flag (`workOffsetIndex = true`) opts a script in, following the
   `coolantModes` / `afterModes` pattern. A script without the flag keeps
   receiving the word for offsets 1-6, so user-loaded posts keep working, and
   is refused by setup name for any offset above 6.
2. **Each post maps the index to its own word** and refuses, by setup name,
   an index it cannot express. The limit becomes the post's, not core's.
3. **The post supplies the display name.** A script may define a function
   (for example `workOffsetName(n)`) returning what the control calls offset
   `n` ("G55", "G54.1 P3", "preset 2"). The UI, setup sheet, MCP tool and
   refusal messages show "WCS n (name)" for the setup's resolved post.
4. **Fallback.** A script that defines no name function shows plain "WCS n".
5. **Core and UI speak indexes.** `WCS_SLOTS` leaves `camcraft-app` and
   `camcraft-ui`, apart from the two pre-v54 file migrations that need the old
   words to read old files.

## Out of scope

- The project file format: it already stores the index, so no version step.
- The legacy `G54` entity name of a document without setups (internal name
  only; renaming it would need a migration for no user benefit).
- Rotated work offsets (#315, #760).

## Open questions

- Where the name lookup lives so the layering holds (ui -> app -> post): an
  app-level function that evaluates the setup's post, with caching, since the
  UI must not evaluate scripts per frame.
- The MCP tool's input: accept an index, and keep accepting the old words as
  aliases for 1-6?
- Whether the six-offset cap is replaced by a per-post maximum the script
  declares, so the combo can list the right number of entries.
- Whether the simulator or any test harness parses the posted offset word
  back; not yet checked.

## Acceptance

- Every existing posted-program golden is byte-identical (the 148 that
  contain a `G5x` word included).
- Every shipped `.cps` declares the flag and maps the index itself; no
  `slotOf`-style parsing of a word remains.
- A setup can be given offset 7 or higher and posts correctly on a dialect
  that supports it; a dialect that does not refuses by setup name.
- A user post without the flag posts offsets 1-6 exactly as before.
- The Setups page shows the resolved post's name for each offset, and
  "WCS n" when the post supplies none.
- `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describe the new
  value, flag and name function.

## Related

Background (closed):

- #196 and #342 introduced the current design: G54-G59 is the setup's post
  label.
- #51 added Heidenhain preset selection for other work offsets - the source
  of the `G5x` -> preset-row regex.
- #876 already called "work offset word" jargon in the UI.

Open work this touches:

- #836 (TinyG post) and #728 (Sienci AltMill on the grblHAL post) add new
  `.cps` files that would need the flag and the mapping.
- #258 (Post dialog) touches the same post-options area.
- #760 (rotated work offset) touches the WCS code; rotation stays out of
  scope here.

title: Reduced-fidelity models: tighten the laws that only refuse today (turning, rotary, multi-axis, cone and engrave rides), the collision laws, and give the import budget a setting

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:multiaxis
labels.description: 3+2, 5-axis, rotary

labels.name: area:turning
labels.description: Lathe and mill-turn

labels.name: area:sim
labels.description: Stock simulation and verification

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
Found while working #864 (a STEP model imported coarser than the importer promises is flagged, its gouge verdicts tightened, and refused past that).

**What #864's PR does.** A reduced-fidelity model carries its achieved error. The gouge laws of the upright mill kinds subtract the excess from their tolerance while a positive tolerance is left: the section law (b), the solid law (b2), the envelope law's gouge half (f), `generate::contain_into`, the lathe's axial hole verdict, and the program sim's deviation tolerance. Past that, the program gate refuses by name.

**What is owed.** Everything below is safe today (refused, or stricter than before), but less useful than it should be.

1. **Kinds refused outright on any reduced-fidelity model**, because their gouge laws do not read the excess yet (`operation::fidelity_law::excess_aware`):
   - the cone and engrave rides: 2D chamfer, deburr, trace, engrave (generator construction laws);
   - probe, and the cross drill (`operation/cross_part.rs`, `SolidLaw { allow: GOUGE_TOL }`);
   - the multi-axis kinds (`motion` `multiaxis/entry_ramp.rs`, `stamp*.rs`, `rotary_links.rs`) and the rotary kinds (`operation/rotary_law.rs`, `allow` and `rapid_allow`);
   - turning (`motion` `turning/revolve.rs`, `form.rs`, `thread.rs`; `blade_warnings`, `thread_warnings`, `form_warnings`);
   - plasma.
   Each needs `material.excess` threaded into its law and the kind added to `excess_aware`. A metre-unit STEP file is always reduced fidelity (next point), so these kinds cannot post on one today.
2. **Collision laws are not tightened**: shank and holder reach (`sim` `verify/reach.rs`), rapids in stock (`verify/rapids.rs`, `rapids_posed.rs`, `rapids_radial.rs`), the turning rapid, bar-feed and holder scans (`margin: GOUGE_TOL` in `generate.rs`). They judge clearance against rest material. While an operation still posts the excess is under 0.01 mm, so a clearance can read up to that much too generous on a convex wall.
3. **A metre-unit STEP file** stops at the kernel's least tolerance (1e-5 m = 0.01 mm, #839) and is flagged reduced fidelity with half the verdict tolerance left. Scaling the geometry to millimetres before meshing would remove the cause.
4. **The facet budget is not a user setting.** The refusal says "re-import with a larger budget" (the maintainer's wording on #864), but `MAX_FACETS` is a constant. The import dialog, the script verb and MCP `import_model` need a budget the user can raise.
5. **Display tolerances** still read the plain 0.01 mm on a reduced-fidelity model: the machined-surface classes (`machined_classes.rs`) and the viewport preview (`ui` `trace/eye.rs`, `cpu_eye.rs`). The binding verdict is tightened; the colours are not.
6. **The envelope law (f) and the containment solid law** are tightened through the same helper as (b) but have no fixture-level pin of their own on a reduced-fidelity model.

Done means: each kind in (1) is either judged with tightened laws or stays refused for a stated reason; the laws in (2) grow their bands by the excess; (3) and (4) are decided and built or closed with the reason; pins for (6).

**Fix:** optional fields `part_number`, `vendor`, `coating`, `helix_deg` and `notes` on the tool, as an additive key so old files load unchanged. Show them in the tool editor and on the setup sheet's tool list, and add them to MCP.

title: No thread-mill tool kind (single- and multi-form) or thread-milling operation

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:2d
labels.description: 2D milling

labels.name: source:agent

labels.name: effort:max
labels.description: New algorithms, formats or open design (issue-worker-max)

labels.name: P6
labels.description: Accepted enhancement, not scheduled

body:
There's no thread-mill tool kind.

**Where:** `ToolKind` (`crates/tools/src/tools.rs:23`) has `Tap` and the lathe `Thread` insert, but no single-form or multi-form thread mill.

**Effect:** thread milling is a common job on small CNC mills (interpolated threads in any material, large or odd sizes, no tap breakage). A vendor tool library can't carry thread mills at all. In one real catalog build, over 300 thread mills had to be left out.

**Fix sketch:**
- New kinds: single-form (one tooth, any pitch within range) and multi-form (several teeth, a fixed pitch). Each carries cutter diameter, form angle, pitch or pitch range, teeth count, neck and shank.
- A thread-milling operation: helical interpolation, internal and external, climb or conventional, single or multi pass, radial passes.
- Simulation and gouge laws for the form.

Effort: max (a new kind, a helical op and the sim).

**Done means:** a thread mill can be stored and used by a thread-milling op that verifies clean and posts helical G2/G3 with Z; pinned with goldens.

# Setups page: two orientation dropdowns (plane + point), same section everywhere

## What

The setup alignment UI is scattered across five separate sections
(preset/angles picker, lay-on-plane row, lay-on-points row, part-axes
rows, work-offset label). Collapse it into ONE section with TWO
dropdowns, drawn identically wherever a setup's orientation is edited:

- **Plane orientation** - how the part's frame is set:
  `Axes` (the two-pick 3D alignment, #769), `Points` (the three-point
  lay, #555), `Face` (the face lay, #330), `Cylinder angle` (NEW: two
  curved-face picks give a bore/cylinder axis; it lands on a chosen
  world axis, turned by an angle about it), `Manual` (the preset combo
  and typed angles, #326/#606).
- **Orientation point** - where the setup's WCS origin sits:
  `From model box` (the parts' bounds - corner or centre), `From stock
  box` (the setup's stock bounds - corner or centre), `Manual point`
  (pick a vertex in the viewport). Placing the point keeps the WCS's
  rotation: the frame comes from the plane dropdown, the point only
  moves the origin.

Selecting an entry expands its controls below the dropdown. Existing
functions are reused verbatim as the expanded content; the completing
work is the cylinder-angle backend and the per-setup origin placement.

## Everywhere the same

The section is one component mounted in BOTH places that edit a
setup's orientation: the Setups overview (every setup stacked) and each
setup's own Settings page. Same dropdowns, same options, same look.

## Done means

- Both pages show the same two dropdowns; picking an option expands
  exactly that option's controls; the old flows still work through
  them (the row functions keep their own entry points, so their
  existing tests stay green untouched).
- `Cylinder angle`: two curved-face picks on a bore land its axis on
  the chosen world axis with the typed angle about it; refusals by
  name (same face twice, coincident centroids, non-finite).
- The orientation point places the named setup's WCS origin (corner /
  centre of the model or stock box, or a picked vertex), rotation kept;
  undo restores. Inactive setups place their own WCS, not the active
  one's.
- UI tests: the section expands, both mount points draw it, the origin
  lands per setup.

body:
# One machining-frame seam: OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame

## What

The part-alignment machinery (#326) and the per-operation tilt frame (the
3+2 index, M5.1 B) both exist and both work — but only separately.
`setup_align::generation_problem` allows generation in an aligned setup for
exactly four kinds (Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive), and tilt
inside an aligned setup is refused outright. Every other planar kind,
picks, and area controls are refused by name. The refusals are a
verification gap, not a mathematical one: the two mechanisms compose as
plain function composition.

This issue builds ONE seam — `OpFrame`, `crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs`
— that composes the two existing mechanisms and becomes the single door
the generators' world reads go through. No generator rewrites: the motion
generators take data (facets, regions, heights); only the app read/wrap
seam moves.

## The frame contract

Coordinate systems:

- **D** — document frame (as modelled). Part entities carry their
  `Location` in D.
- **S** — setup frame: the table frame, also the world the CL stream and
  the post speak. Stock, WCS and fixtures are setup FURNITURE — stored in
  S already (#326's law; their world reads are correct and stay untouched).
- **L** — local machining frame: XY = the cutting plane, +Z = the tool
  axis. Exists only when the op tilts.

Point maps (right-to-left application, the `setup_align::compose`
convention):

- D → S: `A` = the setup's `part_alignment`, baked into part geometry
  reads (`facets_in` and siblings). Never inverted — the CL never maps
  back to D.
- S → L: `T` = `TiltedFrame` from `op.params.tilt()` (`to_local`), applied
  AFTER the alignment read: `p_L = T(A(p_D))`.
- L → S (CL out): `T.to_world`, the tilt's inverse. The whole CL stream
  wraps through `TiltedFrame::world_path`; identity when no tilt exists.

Layers stay separate (never a fourth):

1. part_alignment — setup, physical (how the part is clamped)
2. WCS — program zero (translation today)
3. operation tool orientation — the `Tilt` param

Machine-side relations remain derived internal transforms composed from
these; no user-facing SCS, no second offset frame.

## Design conditions (from the plan review)

1. **Heights and bounding boxes resolve against fully transformed
   geometry** (local bounds of `T(A(f))`), never a bare `z − origin.z`
   shift — a Z shift is not generally correct for an arbitrarily tilted
   plane. `OpFrame`'s height and AABB reads implement this from day one.
2. **Machine capability gates are preserved and pinned by tests**: a
   tilted orientation never silently posts as plain XYZ when the machine
   cannot reach it. The post's tilted-record refusals (non-RTCP, no
   rotary) keep their verdicts.
3. **Stepwise integration**: Phase 1 wires the seam behind the four
   currently-supported kinds, byte-identical. Refusals lift only as their
   numeric tests land: picks in aligned setups next, then further 2D/3D
   families, alignment × tilt last.

## Phases

- **Phase 1 (first branch)**: `OpFrame` + the four kinds through it,
  behavior byte-identical; the seam's math pinned by unit tests (identity,
  90°/180° alignment, alignment × tilt composition, transformed picks,
  local heights on tilted planes, AABBs under arbitrary rotation, CL
  back-transform, tool direction, capability gates, byte-identity).
- **Phase 2**: the selection walk reads picked parts through the seam
  (`facets_in`); picks in aligned setups verified. Tilt × picks stays
  refused.
- **Phase 3**: `verified_kind` extended kind by kind (whole-model 3D
  kinds first), each with a pinned numeric test; area controls; then tilt
  × alignment.
- **Phase 4**: re-evaluate #760 (rotated-offset carry) on top of the
  unified seam — normal 3-axis work needs alignment coverage, not offset
  rotation.

## Done means (Phase 1)

- `crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs` exists with the contract above;
  `collect_job` reads geometry/heights for the four kinds through it.
- The mandatory test list above is green.
- Existing aligned-setup tests (#326's) and goldens pass unchanged —
  byte-identical output.
- No refusal lifted, no post change, no generator change.

Related: #326 (part alignment), #316 (setup-to-setup transform), #315
(rotation refusal at the post), #760 (rotated-offset carry — re-evaluated
in phase 4, untouched by this issue's branches).

title: Setup page alignment: one clear flow, moves apply to the body as it is, and picks you can actually see

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: area:ui
labels.description: User interface and picking

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P3
labels.description: Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround; fix now

body:
Reported by the maintainer while hand-testing the setup page's part alignment (screenshot of the Setups page attached in chat: Part alignment dropdown at the top, then "Lay on a plane - pick a face", "pick three points", "Axes in the plane - pick an edge or two points").

## What's wrong

1. **The "Part alignment" control at the top overrides the pickers.** The dropdown and the Turn X/Y/Z + about + Apply row sit above the face, three-point and edge/two-point pickers, and applying one wipes out what the others did. It's unclear which one is in charge. The page should read as one flow, where the pickers are the way to align and the preset/turn row doesn't silently override them (or is clearly a separate "start from a preset" step).
2. **Each pick-driven move resets the part and then moves it.** Laying on a face, on three points or applying axes first returns the body to its import pose and then applies only the new transform. Expected: each move applies **to the body as it is now** (incremental, composed with what was done before), and undo steps back one move at a time.
3. **Pick status shows internal ids.** "Face 0xccc7c…" (the welded-face id) means nothing to a user. Show the count and the kind: "1 face selected", "2 points selected", "1 edge selected".
4. **Picked geometry is hard to see.**
   - **Faces:** only the outline is drawn in purple. Fill the whole picked face with the pick colour (semi-transparent), so it's obvious which face it is.
   - **Vertices / points:** draw them as round, visible markers (filled discs, somewhat transparent is fine), not a speck.
   - **Edges:** the picked edge line is so thin it barely shows against the grey part. Draw it noticeably thicker (bold).

## Related
- #692 (one picking rule for the whole app: what is pickable). This issue is about how picks are *shown* and how the alignment page *applies* them.
- #330, #555, #557, #606 (lay on a face, three-point plane, axes by edge/two points, align about the WCS origin): the features this page combines.
- #701 (WCS from picked features with roles).

## Done means
- Applying a face, three-point or axis alignment moves the part from its current pose; a pinning test applies two alignments in a row and checks the second composes on the first, and undo restores each step.
- The top "Part alignment" preset/turn row no longer silently discards a picker's result (pinned by a test, or the page is restructured so the two can't conflict); the flow is described in the page's tooltips.
- Pick status reads "N face(s)/edge(s)/point(s) selected", with no internal ids (structural test).
- Picked faces are filled with the pick colour, picked points are round markers, and picked edges are drawn bold. Checked by the structural/paint assertions where they can be, hand-tested by the maintainer otherwise (no snapshot PNG changes in the PR).

title: Process changes - fork maintainers please subscribe

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: P?
labels.description: Paused: never picked until the maintainer sets a real priority

body:
**Subscribe to this issue** (the "Subscribe" button on the right) if you work from a fork of CamCraft, especially with an AI agent.

Forks sync product code only at release tags (AGENTS.md "A fork syncs from upstream at each cut tag"). But the *process* - `AGENTS.md`, the agent definitions in `.claude/agents/`, the skills in `.claude/skills/` and `scripts/gate.*` - changes between releases, and a fork's agents should follow the current rules (review labels, priority labels, release steps, and so on).

**How it works:**
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` holds one number. Every PR that changes a process file bumps it.
- Every such PR also adds a comment **here**: the new version, what changed, and what to pull. Subscribers get one notification per change.
- A fork's agent compares its `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` with upstream's at the start of each session and, if upstream is newer, pulls just the process files (AGENTS.md "Process files sync on every session"). Product code still waits for the next release tag.

**To pull by hand:**
```
git fetch upstream
git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh
git commit -m "chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION <n>"
```

This issue stays open and pinned. It's labelled `P?` so no agent ever picks it up as work.

title: Launch terminal is silent while the app works - add real debug logging (tracing) to stdout

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: area:build
labels.description: Build, CI, release, tests

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

labels.name: effort:high
labels.description: Several crates, new behaviour with tests; safety floor (issue-worker-high)

labels.name: P5
labels.description: Agent surface and tooling keep up with what shipped

body:
## What happens
When CamCraft is started from a terminal, the terminal tells you almost nothing
about what the app is doing. There is no logging framework in the workspace at
all: no `log` or `tracing` dependency in any Cargo.toml, no subscriber
init in the binaries - just ~185 ad-hoc `println!`/`eprintln!` calls scattered
across crates (cli.rs, gpu_init.rs, shell.rs, the post bin). If a subsystem
decides, refuses, retries, or fails to write a file, no line reaches the
console and the failure is only discovered later by forensics on the output.

## Why now (session of 2026-11-07)
Two incidents this week were diagnosed only by reading source afterwards,
because the console was silent during them:
- **A file did not get saved when post processing** - the post appeared to
  succeed; nothing in the terminal said which path it wrote (or that it wrote
  nothing at all).
- **A limit was hit while generating operations** - the generator aborted on a
  budget/limit; the terminal showed no trace of which cap fired or what the
  result was downgraded to.

Prime Directive says "log diagnostics, never silence" - today we cannot.

## Expected
The launching terminal streams debug-level logs of app activity, filterable:
- project save / post write: source path, destination, bytes, or the reason
  nothing was written;
- operation generation: start, end, duration, which limits/budgets stopped a
  generator and what fallback took over;
- verify/sim refusals: the rule that fired and the numbers behind it;
- commands executing (name + affected entities) at debug level.

## Suggested shape
`tracing` + `tracing_subscriber` fmt layer writing to stderr at startup of the
UI binary, default level `info`, overridable by `RUST_LOG` (or a camcraft
config/env of our own). Instrument the command dispatch seam, generators, and
post entry points - the crates are already split (M4.1), so each takes its own
span targets (`camcraft_app::post`, `camcraft_motion::adaptive`, ...). Keep
hot generation loops behind level gates - logging must not slow generation.

## Done means
- Launching the app and running a post writes terminal lines naming the file
  path and result; a failed/skipped write says why.
- Hitting a generation budget (e.g. an Adaptive limit) prints which limit and
  what happened next.
- Levels are controlled by env var, default output stays quiet at `info`, and
  the batch gate shows no measurable generation slowdown.

Found while debugging the post-save incident (user request, 2026-11-07).
